254.e: Ultimately Lakshman deprived Atkaaye, the specialist in many sciences of weapons and arms, of his weapons and arms

254.g: ਹੱਯ ਮੁਕਟ ਸੂਤ ਬਿਨੁ ਭਯੋ ਗਵਾਰ ॥
254.t: ha'y mukaT soot bin bhayo gavaar ||

254.g: ਕਛੁ ਚਪੇ ਚੋਰ ਜਿਮ ਬਲ ਸੰਭਾਰ ॥੫੧੩॥
254.t: kachh chape chor jim bal sa(n)bhaar ||513||
254.e: He was deprived of his horse, crown and garments and he tried ot conceal himself like a thief mustering his strength.513.

254.g: ਸਮ ਚਲੇ ਕਾਲ ਕੀ ਜੁਆਲ ਤਾਤ ॥
254.t: sam chale kaal kee juaal taat ||
254.e: He discharged arrows causing destruction like Indra’s Vajra and they were striking like the advancing fire of death

254.g: ਜਨ ਪ੍ਰਲੈ ਕਾਲ ਕੋ ਮੇਘ ਜੈਸ ॥੫੧੪॥
254.t: jan pralai kaal ko megh jais ||514||
254.e: The hero Atkaaye become highly infuriated like the clouds of doomsday.514.
He began to prattle like a man without the energy of a youth, clinging to a woman without satisfying her,

254.g: ਜਿਮ ਦੰਤ ਰਹਤ ਗਹ ਸ੍ਵਾਨ ਸਸਕ ॥
254.t: jim dha(n)t rahat geh savaiaan sasak ||

254.g: ਜਿਮ ਗਏ ਬੈਸ ਬਲ ਬੀਰਜ ਰਸਕ ॥੫੧੫॥
254.t: jim ge bais bal beeraj rasak ||515||
254.e: Or like a teethless dog on catching a rabbit whom he can do no harm, or like a libertine without the semen.515.

254.g: ਜਿਮ ਦਰਬ ਹੀਣ ਕਛੁ ਕਰਿ ਬਪਾਰ ॥
254.t: jim dharab heen kachh kar bapaar ||

254.e: Atkaaye was in such a situation which is experienced by a trader without money or a warriors without weapons.

254.g: ਜਣ ਬਾਜ ਹੀਣ ਰਥ ਕੋ ਚਲਾਵ ॥੫੧੬॥
254.t: jan baaj heen rath ko chalaav ||516||
254.e: He looked like and ugly prostitute or a chariot without horses.516.
Then the benevolent Lakshman stuck his sharp-edged sword and chopped the demon into two halves.
That warriors named Atkaaye fell in the battlefield and on seeing him (falling) many warriors fled away.517.

254.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਰਾਮਵਤਾਰ ਅਤਕਾਇ ਬਧਹਿ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੧੪॥
254.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake raamavataar atakai badheh dhiaai samaapatam sat ||14||
254.e: End of the chapter entitled ‘Killing of Atkaaye’ in Ramavtar in BACHITTAR NATAK.
Now begins the description of the war with Makrachh :
PAADHRI STANZA

254.g: ਕਹ ਜਾਹੁ ਰਾਮ ਨਹੀ ਪੈਹੋ ਜਾਨ ॥
254.t: keh jaahu raam nahee paiho jaan ||
254.e: After that Makrachh joined the army and said. “O Ram! You cannot save yourself now

254.g: ਜਿਨ ਹਤਯੋ ਤਾਤ ਰਣ ਮੋ ਅਖੰਡ ॥
254.t: jin hatayo taat ran mo akha(n)dd ||

254.g: ਸੋ ਲਰੋ ਆਨ ਮੋ ਸੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡ ॥੫੧੮॥
254.t: so laro aan mo so(n) pracha(n)dd ||518||
254.e: He who has killed my father, that mighty warriors should come forward and wage war with me.”518.
Ram heard these crooked words and in great rage he held his weapons and arms in his hands

254.g: ਬਹੁ ਤਾਣ ਬਾਣ ਤਿਹ ਹਣੇ ਅੰਗ ॥
254.t: bahu taan baan teh hane a(n)g ||

254.e: He pulled (his bow) discharged his arrows, and fearlessly killed Makrachh.519.

254.g: ਜਬ ਹਤੇ ਬੀਰ ਅਰ ਹਣੀ ਸੈਨ ॥
254.t: jab hate beer ar hanee sain ||

254.g: ਤਬ ਭਜੌ ਸੂਰ ਹੁਐ ਕਰ ਨਿਚੈਨ ॥
254.t: tab bhajau soor huaai kar nichain ||
254.e: When this hero and his army were killed, then all the warriors, becoming weaponsless, ran away (from the filed)

254.g: ਦਲ ਰੁੱਕਯੋ ਰਾਮ ਕੋ ਤਯਾਗ ਕਾਨ ॥੫੨੦॥
254.t: dhal ru'kayo raam ko tayaag kaan ||520||
254.e: After that Kumbh and Ankumbh came forward and obstructed the army of Ram.520.
AJBA STANZA
The horses jumped, the warriors thundered and began to strike blows, being bedecked with weapons and arms.521.
The bows broke, the arrows were discharged, the warriors became firm and the shafts were showered.522.

255.e: The warriors wandered after getting wounded and their zeal grew, with fury, they began to lose their senses.523.
The warriors covered with armours, began to fight in the battlefield and fell down unconscious.524.
The demons army sped away feeling ashamed.525.
The brave fighters fell and their faces shone
They wedded the heavenly damsels and fulfilled their wishes.526.

255.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਰਾਮਵਤਾਰ ਮਕਰਾਛ ਕੁੰਭ ਅਨਕੁੰਭ ਬਧਹਿ ਧਯਾਇ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ॥
255.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake raamavataar makaraachh ku(n)bh anaku(n)bh badheh dhayai samaapatam sat ||
255.e: End of the chapter entitled ‘Killing of Makrachh, Kumbh and Ankumbh’ in Ramavtar in BACHITTAR NATAK.
Now begins the description of the war with Ravna :
Ravna heard about the victory (of Ram), he being highly infuriated in his mind, began to shout violently.527.
Seeing his citadel besieged his ire grew more and he saw women running away in fear.528.
All the women are running away in illusion and Ravana obstructed them catching their hair.529.
They were lamenting profusely and praying to God and were asking for forgiveness for their sins.530.
That persistent Ravana got up on listening to such sounds and it seemed that a fire cauldron was blazing.531.
He began to kill the human army and with his arrows all the directions were obstructed.532.
The arrows were discharged and the warriors were wounded.
The shields were slipping down and the fires blazed.533.

256.e: The helmets were knocked and the wounds were caused, the warriors were infuriated and their zeal grew.534.
The fast-moving horses began to run and the warriors obtained salvation after severe fighting.535.
The elephants ran like deer and the warriors took refuge with their comrades
The enemies ran and felt shy of fighting.536.
The bodies and the armours were cut, the ears and eyes were amputated.537.
The warriors breathed their last and ferried across the world-ocean, some were burnt in the fire of ire and took rufuge.538.
The gods moved in their air-vehicles and saw the scene
The heavenly damsels wandered and began to wed the warriors.539.
Various types of musical instruments resounded and the elephants thundered
The warriors took refuge while some began to fight.,540.
The arrows began to kill warriors and the fire came out of the shelds.541.
The horses began to run and the warriors began to roar
They began to kill one another and ferry across the worls-ocean.542.
After gaining victory in war, the enemies were being made allies,
The cleavage was caused amongst the warriors and they were also being forsaken.543.
The king Ravana thundered violently and with great zeal marched forward.544.
The warriors began to fall after being saturated with blood and th blood was flowing like water.545.
There is lot of discipline and lot of obstruction

257.e: The limbs are being chopped in the war. 546
There is lot of discipline and lot of obstruction
The limbs are being chopped in the war.547.
The sky is becoming full of heavenly damsels.548.
The warriors are pulling bows and discharging arrows.549.
The musical instruments are resounding, the warriors are thundering and are falling on the ground after swinging.550.
The sky is torn with arrows and the eyes of the warriors are getting red
The knocking on the shields is being heard and the rising flames re being seen.551.

258.e: The warriors saturated with blood, are falling down on the earth and the heavenly damsels are roaming
The sky is filled with the sounds of conches, other tunes and drums.552.
The armours of the warriors have been torn and they are fighting in the war
The brave fighters are confronting one another and the heavenly damsels are dancing  there is talk of war on the earth.553.
The headless trunks arose in the war and were opening their gauzy armour
With garbs like lions the warriors are highly infuriated and their hair have loosened.554.
The helmets have broken and the kings have fled away
The warriors, having been wounded, are falling on the earth after swinging and with a bang they are falling.555.
The large trumpets have resounded and the bedecked warriors are being seen
They are dying in the war being chopped in bits and being intoxicated in war-frenzy, they are becoming unconscious.556.
Innumerable weapons and arms are being used and the earth is coloured with blood upto a great distance
The weapons are being struck indiscreetly and the terrible warriors are shouting.557.
The clusters of corpses are lying scattered  the warriors are engrossed in a horrible war on one side and on the other, some of them are running away.
The ghosts and friends are laughing in the cemeteries and here the brave fighters are fighting after receiving blows of swords.558.
BAHRAA STANZA

258.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਰੋਸ ਕਰ ਰਾਜ ਪਖਰੀਆ ਧਾਵਹੀ ॥
258.t: adhik ros kar raaj pakhareeaa dhaavahee ||

258.g: ਰਾਮ ਰਾਮ ਬਿਨੁ ਸੰਕ ਪੁਕਾਰਤ ਆਵਹੀ ॥
258.t: raam raam bin sa(n)k pukaarat aavahee ||
258.e: The demon warriors wearing armours, march forward in great fury, but on reaching within the forces of Ram, they become like followers of Ram and begin to shout the name of Ram

258.g: ਰੁੱਝ ਜੁੱਝ ਝੜ ਪੜਤ ਭਯਾਨਕ ਭੂਮ ਪਰ ॥
258.t: ru'jh ju'jh jhaR paRat bhayaanak bhoom par ||

258.g: ਰਾਮਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਕੇ ਹਾਥ ਗਏ ਭਵਸਿੰਧ ਤਰ ॥੫੫੯॥
258.t: raamacha(n)dhr ke haath ge bhavasi(n)dh tar ||559||
258.e: While fighting they fall down on the earth in a dreadful posture and ferring across the world-ocean at the hands of Ram.559.

258.g: ਸਿਮਟ ਸਾਗ ਸੰਗ੍ਰਹੈ ਸਮੁਹ ਹੁਐ ਜੂਝਹੀ ॥
258.t: simaT saag sa(n)grahai samuh huaai joojhahee ||

258.g: ਟੂਕ ਟੂਕ ਹੁਐ ਗਿਰਤ ਨ ਘਰ ਕਹ ਬੂਝਹੀ ॥
258.t: Took Took huaai girat na ghar keh boojhahee ||
258.e: After revolving and holding the lance the warriors come forward and fight and fall down on being chopped into bits

258.g: ਖੰਡ ਖੰਡ ਹੁਐ ਗਿਰਤ ਖੰਡ ਧਨ ਖੰਡ ਰਨ ॥
258.t: kha(n)dd kha(n)dd huaai girat kha(n)dd dhan kha(n)dd ran ||

258.g: ਤਨਕ ਤਨਕ ਲਗ ਜਾਹਿ ਅਸਨ ਕੀ ਧਾਰ ਤਨ ॥੫੬੦॥
258.t: tanak tanak lag jaeh asan kee dhaar tan ||560||
258.e: On receiving only the small blows of the edge of swords the brave fighters fall down in numerous part.560.
SANGEET BAHRA STANZA

258.g: ਸਾਗੜਦੀ ਸਾਗ ਸੰਗ੍ਰਹੈ ਤਾਗੜਦੀ ਰਣ ਤੁਰੀ ਨਚਾਵਹਿ ॥
258.t: saagaRadhee saag sa(n)grahai taagaRadhee ran turee nachaaveh ||

258.g: ਝਾਗੜਦੀ ਝੂਮ ਗਿਰ ਭੂਮਿ ਸਾਗੜਦੀ ਸੁਰਪੁਰਹਿ ਸਿਧਾਵਹਿ ॥
258.t: jhaagaRadhee jhoom gir bhoom saagaRadhee surapureh sidhaaveh ||
258.e: Holding the lances the warriors are causing them to dance in the war and after swinging and falling on the earth, they are leaving for the abode of gods

258.g: ਆਗੜਦੀ ਅੰਗ ਹੁਐ ਭੰਗ ਆਗੜਦੀ ਆਹਵ ਮਹਿ ਡਿਗਹੀ ॥
258.t: aagaRadhee a(n)g huaai bha(n)g aagaRadhee aahav meh ddigahee ||

258.g: ਹੋ ਬਾਗੜਦੀ ਵੀਰ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਾਰ ਸਾਗੜਦੀ ਸ੍ਰੋਣਤ ਤਨ ਭਿਗਹੀ ॥੫੬੧॥
258.t: ho baagaRadhee veer bikraar saagaRadhee sronat tan bhigahee ||561||
258.e: The brave fighters are falling with chopped limbs in the battlefield and their dreadful bodies are saturated with blood.561.

258.g: ਰਾਗੜਦੀ ਰੋਸ ਰਿਪ ਰਾਜ ਲਾਗੜਦੀ ਲਛਮਣ ਪੈ ਧਾਯੋ ॥
258.t: raagaRadhee ros rip raaj laagaRadhee lachhaman pai dhaayo ||

258.g: ਕਾਗੜਦੀ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਤਨ ਕੁੜਯੋ ਪਾਗੜਦੀ ਹੁਐ ਪਵਨ ਸਿਧਾਯੋ ॥
258.t: kaagaRadhee krodh tan kuRayo paagaRadhee huaai pavan sidhaayo ||
258.e: The enemy-king Ravana fell in great fury on lakshman and went towards him with wind speed and great ire

258.g: ਆਗੜਦੀ ਅਨੁਜ ਉਰ ਤਾਤ ਘਾਗੜਦੀ ਗਹਿ ਘਾਇ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰਯੋ ॥
258.t: aagaRadhee anuj ur taat ghaagaRadhee geh ghai prahaarayo ||

258.g: ਝਾਗੜਦੀ ਝੂਮਿ ਭੂਅ ਗਿਰਯੋ ਸਾਗੜਦੀ ਸੁਤ ਬੈਰ ਉਤਾਰਯੋ ॥੫੬੨॥
258.t: jhaagaRadhee jhoom bhooa girayo saagaRadhee sut bair utaarayo ||562||
258.e: He inflicted a wound on the heart of Lakshman and in this way wreaking vengeance on him for the killing of his son, he cused the fall of Lakshman.562.

258.g: ਚਾਗੜਦੀ ਚਿੰਕ ਚਾਵਡੀ ਡਾਗੜਦੀ ਡਾਕਣ ਡੱਕਾਰੀ ॥
258.t: chaagaRadhee chi(n)k chaavaddee ddaagaRadhee ddaakan dda'kaaree ||
258.e: The vultures shriked and the vampires belched

258.g: ਭਾਗੜਦੀ ਭੂਤ ਭਰ ਹਰੇ ਰਾਗੜਦੀ ਰਣ ਰੋਸ ਪ੍ਰਜਾਰੀ ॥
258.t: bhaagaRadhee bhoot bhar hare raagaRadhee ran ros prajaaree ||
258.e: Burning in this fire of fury in the battlefield the ghosts and others were filled with joy

258.g: ਮਾਗੜਦੀ ਮੂਰਛਾ ਭਯੋ ਲਾਗੜਦੀ ਲਛਮਣ ਰਣ ਜੁਝਯੋ ॥
258.t: maagaRadhee moorachhaa bhayo laagaRadhee lachhaman ran jujhayo ||
258.e: Lakshman while fighting in the field became unconscious and Ram,

259.g: ਜਾਗੜਦੀ ਜਾਣ ਜੁਝਿ ਗਯੋ ਰਾਗੜਦੀ ਰਘੁਪਤ ਇਮ ਬੁਝਯੋ ॥੫੬੩॥
259.t: jaagaRadhee jaan jujh gayo raagaRadhee raghupat im bujhayo ||563||
259.e: The king of Raghava clan, considering him dead, became pale.563.

259.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਰਾਮਵਤਾਰ ਲਛਮਨ ਮੂਰਛਨਾ ਭਵੇਤ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ॥
259.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake raamavataar lachhaman moorachhanaa bhavet dhiaai samaapatam sat ||
259.e: End of the chapter entitled ‘Lakshman becoming Unconscious’ in Ramvtar in BACHITTAR NATAK.
SANGEET BAHRAA STANZA

259.g: ਕਾਗੜਦੀ ਕਟਕ ਕਪਿ ਭਜਯੋ ਲਾਗੜਦੀ ਲਛਮਣ ਜੁੱਝਯੋ ਜਬ ॥
259.t: kaagaRadhee kaTak kap bhajayo laagaRadhee lachhaman ju'jhayo jab ||

259.g: ਰਾਗੜਦੀ ਰਾਮ ਰਿਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਸਾਗੜਦੀ ਗਹਿ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਭ ॥
259.t: raagaRadhee raam ris bharayo saagaRadhee geh asatr sasatr sabh ||
259.e: The force of monkeys ran helter-skelter when Lakshman fell down and catching hold of his weapons and arms in his hand Ram was highly infuriated

259.g: ਧਾਗੜਦੀ ਧਉਲ ਧੜ ਹੜਯੋ ਕਾਗੜਦੀ ਕੋੜੰਭ ਕੜੱਕਯੋ ॥
259.t: dhaagaRadhee dhaul dhaR haRayo kaagaRadhee koRa(n)bh kaRa'kayo ||

259.g: ਭਾਗੜਦੀ ਭੂੰਮਿ ਭੜਹੜੀ ਪਾਗੜਦੀ ਜਨ ਪਲੈ ਪਲੱਟਯੋ ॥੫੬੪॥
259.t: bhaagaRadhee bhoo(n)m bhaRahaRee paagaRadhee jan palai pala'Tayo ||564||
259.e: With the clattering sound of the weapons of Ram, the Bull, the support of the earth trembled and the earth shook as if the doomsday had arrived.564.
ARDH NARAAJ STANZA
The double-edged swords came out and Ram seemed greatly impressive
The sound of the kettle-drums was heard and the imprisoned people began to cry.565.
A queer scene was created and the forces of men and monkey fell on the demon forces with sharp nails like the rising clouds of the month of Sawan.566.
The warriors are roaming on all the four sides for the destruction of sins and are challenging one another
The brave fighters are leaving their bodies the gods are shouting “Bravo, Bravo”.567.
The sharp arrows are being discharged and the terrible kettle-drums are resounding
The intoxicating sounds are being heard from all the four sides.568.
Shiva and his Ganas (attendants) are seen dancing and it seems that the female ghosts are laughing and bowing their heads before Parvati.569.
ANOOP NIRAAJ STANZA
The vampires are roaming and the horses are moving creating a circular spectacle
The warriors are being made prisoners and are hailing.570.
There are knockings of the blows of the swords on the shields and with the arrows being discharged by the kings the humans and monkeys are falling on the earth.571.
On the other side the monkeys are shrieking
On account of what the demons are fleeing   the sounds of arrows and other weapons are creating the terrible and tumultuous resonance.572.
The groups of ghosts are feeling frightened and perplexed
The armoured horses and roaring elephants are moving in the battlefield.573.
The gods are also becoming fearful on seeing the terrible war of the warriors

260.e: The white swords and sharp arrows are being showered.574.
Ram saw his brother Lakshman fighting,
And he discharged the arrows touching the sky.575.
These arrows chopped the riders on chariots and horses, but still the warriors stood firmly in the field
Ram killed the brave fighters who were wedded by the heavenly damsels.576.
In this way the war was conquered and in this war many warriors fled away
Wherever the brave fighters saw one another, they cleared the account only on sacrificing their lives.577.
The army felt ashamed on remembering the defeat

260.g: ਸਾਗੜਦੰਗ ਸੁਗ੍ਰੀਵ ਤੇ ਆਦਿ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥
260.t: saagaRadha(n)g sugreev te aadh lai kai ||

260.e: Sugriva and others got highly enraged.578.
Hanuman was also greatly infuriated and he stood firmly in the battlefield

260.g: ਤਾਗੜਦੰਗ ਤੈ ਕੈ ਹਨੂ ਤਉ ਪੁਕਾਰੇ ॥੫੭੯॥
260.t: taagaRadha(n)g tai kai hanoo tau pukaare ||579||
260.e: All those who fought with him suffered defeat and for this reason Hanuman is called the “killer of all”.579.
Hanuman said to Ram, “Kindly stretch your hand towards me and bless me,

261.g: ਹਰੋ ਆਜ ਪਾਨੰ ਸੁਰੰ ਮੋਹ ਲੋਕੋ ॥੫੮੦॥
261.t: haro aaj paana(n) sura(n) moh loko ||580||
261.e: “By patting me on my back and I shall conquer all the abodes of gods today.”580.
Uttering these words Hanuman flew and it seemed that he had become one with the sky.
Ram sat down disappointed, keeping the hope in his mind.581.
Whosoever came in front of Hanuman, he killed him,
And thus killing (the forces) he reached on the bank of a tank.582.
There a terrible-looking demon was hiding

261.g: ਆਗੜਦੰਗ ਹੈ ਏਕ ਤੇ ਏਕ ਜੂਟੀ ॥੫੮੩॥
261.t: aagaRadha(n)g hai ek te ek jooTee ||583||
261.e: And at the same place Hanuman saw many herbs clustered with one another.583.
The highly radiant Hanuman, seeing this, was perturbed and felt confused about the herb to be taken away
He uprooted the whole mountain and returned with the medicinal herbs.584.
He reached that battlefield with the mountain where Lakshman was lying unconscious
The apothecary Sushan put the required herb in the month of Lakshman.585.
The mighty warrior Lakshman regained his senses and the roaming heavenly damsels went back
The great trumpets resounded in the battlefield.586.
The arrows were discharged and the warriors began to fight again with one another.
The brave fighters dying in the battlefield became true martyrs.587.
KALAS
The terrible warriors were absorbed in fighting the ghosts, fiends and Baitals began to dance
The blows were struck with many hands creating knocking sounds and the white edges of the swords glittered.588.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

261.g: ਉੱਜਲ ਅਸ ਧਾਰੰ ਲਸਤ ਅਪਾਰੰ ਕਰਣ ਲੁਝਾਰੰ ਛਬਿ ਧਾਰੰ ॥
261.t: au'jal as dhaara(n) lasat apaara(n) karan lujhaara(n) chhab dhaara(n) ||
261.e: The white edges of the swords, increasing splendour, looked impressive

261.g: ਸੋਭਿਤ ਜਿਮੁ ਆਰੰ ਅਤ ਛਬਿ ਧਾਰੰ ਸੁ ਬਧ ਸੁਧਾਰੰ ਅਰ ਗਾਰੰ ॥
261.t: sobhit jim aara(n) at chhab dhaara(n) su badh sudhaara(n) ar gaara(n) ||
261.e: These sword are the destroyers of the enemies and appear like saws

261.g: ਜੈਪੱਤ੍ਰੰ ਦਾਤੀ ਮਦਿਣੰ ਮਾਤੀ ਸ੍ਰੋਣੰ ਰਾਤੀ ਜੈ ਕਰਣੰ ॥
261.t: jaipa'tra(n) dhaatee madhina(n) maatee srona(n) raatee jai karana(n) ||
261.e: They frighten the enemy by granting victory, by bathing in the blood,

261.g: ਦੁੱਜਨ ਦਲ ਹੰਤੀ ਅਛਲ ਜਯੰਤੀ ਕਿਲਵਿਖ ਹੰਤੀ ਭੈ ਹਰਣੰ ॥੫੮੯॥
261.t: dhu'jan dhal ha(n)tee achhal jaya(n)tee kilavikh ha(n)tee bhai harana(n) ||589||
261.e: By destroying the intoxicated tyrants and by perishing all the vices.589.
KALAS
There was consternation, the warriors ran and their bodies wearing armour trembled
The trumpets resounded violently in the war and seeing the mighty warriors the heavenly damsels advanced towards them again.590.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

261.g: ਘੁੰਮੀ ਰਣ ਹੂਰੰ ਨਭ ਝੜ ਪੂਰੰ ਲਖ ਲਖ ਸੂਰੰ ਮਨ ਮੋਹੀ ॥
261.t: ghu(n)mee ran hoora(n) nabh jhaR poora(n) lakh lakh soora(n) man mohee ||
261.e: Returning from heaven the damsels moved towards the warriors and enchanted their mind

261.g: ਆਰੁਣ ਤਨ ਬਾਣੰ ਛਬ ਅਪ੍ਰਮਾਣੰ ਅਤਿਦੁਤ ਖਾਣੰ ਤਨ ਸੋਹੀ ॥
261.t: aarun tan baana(n) chhab apramaana(n) atidhut khaana(n) tan sohee ||
261.e: Their bodies were red like the arrows saturated with blood and their beauty was unparalleled

262.g: ਕਾਛਨੀ ਸੁਰੰਗੰ ਛਬਿ ਅੰਗ ਅੰਗੰ ਲਜਤ ਅਨੰਗੰ ਲਖ ਰੂਪੰ ॥
262.t: kaachhanee sura(n)ga(n) chhab a(n)g a(n)ga(n) lajat ana(n)ga(n) lakh roopa(n) ||
262.e: Seeing the beauty of these heavenly damsels, who were wearing elegantly coloured raiments, t

262.g: ਸਾਇਕ ਦ੍ਰਿਗ ਹਰਣੀ ਕੁਮਤ ਪ੍ਰਜਰਣੀ ਬਰਬਰ ਬਰਣੀ ਬੁਧ ਕੂਪੰ ॥੫੯੧॥
262.t: saik dhirag haranee kumat prajaranee barabar baranee budh koopa(n) ||591||
262.e: He cupid was felling shy and these were the intellingent heavenly damsels, doe-eyed, destroyers of bad intellect and wedders of mighty warriors.591.
KALAS
Their faces were like lotus, eyes like deer and utterance like nightingale, these heavenly damsels were stores of elegance
With gait of elephants, with slim waists of lion and were captivators of mind with the side glances of their eyes.592.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

262.g: ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਨੈਣੀ ਸੁਰ ਪਿਕ ਬੈਣੀ ਚਿਤ ਹਰ ਲੈਣੀ ਗਜ ਗੈਣੰ ॥
262.t: su(n)dhar mirag nainee sur pik bainee chit har lainee gaj gaina(n) ||
262.e: They have splendid eyes, their utterance is sweet like nightingale and they captivate the mind like the gait of the elephant

262.g: ਮਾਧੁਰ ਬਿਧਿ ਬਦਨੀ ਸੁਬੁੱਧਿਨ ਸਦਨੀ ਕੁਮਤਿਨ ਕਦਨੀ ਛਬਿ ਮੈਣੰ ॥
262.t: maadhur bidh badhanee subu'dhin sadhanee kumatin kadhanee chhab maina(n) ||
262.e: They are all-pervading, have charming faces, with elegance of the god of love, they are the store-house of good intellect, the destroyer of evil intellect,

262.g: ਅੰਗਕਾ ਸੁਰੰਗੀ ਨਟਵਰ ਰੰਗੀ ਝਾਝ ਉਤੰਗੀ ਪਗ ਧਾਰੰ ॥
262.t: a(n)gakaa sura(n)gee naTavar ra(n)gee jhaajh uta(n)gee pag dhaara(n) ||
262.e: Have godly limbs  they stand slantingly on one side, wear anklets in their feet,

262.g: ਬੇਸਰ ਗਜਰਾਰੰ ਪਹੂਚ ਅਪਾਰੰ ਕਚਿ ਘੁੰਘਰਾਰੰ ਆਹਾਰੰ ॥੫੯੩॥
262.t: besar gajaraara(n) pahooch apaara(n) kach ghu(n)gharaara(n) aahaara(n) ||593||
262.e: Ivory-ornament in their nose and have black curly hair.593.
KALAS
These heavenly damsels of elegant cheeks and unique beauty, have wreaths of gems on various parts of their bodies

262.g: ਨਿਰਖ ਮਦਨ ਦੁਤ ਹੋਤ ਸੁ ਮਾਰੰ ॥੫੯੪॥
262.t: nirakh madhan dhut hot su maara(n) ||594||
262.e: The bracelets of their hands are spreading brightness and seeing such elegance the beauty of the god of love is getting dim.594.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

262.g: ਸੋਭਿਤ ਛਬਿ ਧਾਰੰ ਕਚ ਘੁੰਘਰਾਰੰ ਰਸਨ ਰਸਾਰੰ ਉਜਿਆਰੰ ॥
262.t: sobhit chhab dhaara(n) kach ghu(n)gharaara(n) rasan rasaara(n) ujiaara(n) ||

262.g: ਪਹੁੰਚੀ ਗਜਰਾਰੰ ਸੁਬਿਧ ਸੁਧਾਰੰ ਮੁਕਤ ਨਿਹਾਰੰ ਉਰ ਧਾਰੰ ॥
262.t: pahu(n)chee gajaraara(n) subidh sudhaara(n) mukat nihaara(n) ur dhaara(n) ||
262.e: With black hair sweet speech they appear very impressive and moving freely, they are roaming within the jostling of the elephants.

262.g: ਸੋਹਤ ਚਖ ਚਾਰੰ ਰੰਗ ਰੰਗਾਰੰ ਬਿਬਿਧ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਰੰ ਅਤਿ ਆਂਜੇ ॥
262.t: sohat chakh chaara(n) ra(n)g ra(n)gaara(n) bibidh prakaara(n) at aa(n)je ||

262.g: ਬਿਖ ਧਰ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਜੈਸੇ ਜਲ ਜਨ ਵੈਸੇ ਸਸੀਅਰ ਜੈਸੇ ਸਰ ਮਾਜੇ ॥੫੯੫॥
262.t: bikh dhar mirag jaise jal jan vaise saseear jaise sar maaje ||595||
262.e: With antimony in their eyes and dyed in various coulurs they look splendid with their beautiful eyes. In this way, their eyes, assaulting like poisonous serpents, but innocent like deer, they are winsome like lotus and moon.595.
KALAS
The foolish Ravana was highly infuriated in the war  when the terrible war began amidst violent resonance,

262.g: ਅਰ ਦਲ ਮੱਧਿ ਸਬਦ ਕਰ ਉੱਧੰ ॥੫੯੬॥
262.t: ar dhal ma'dh sabadh kar u'dha(n) ||596||
262.e: All the warriors began to fight and roam shouting violently among the enemy forces.596.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

262.g: ਧਾਯੋ ਕਰ ਕ੍ਰੁੱਧੰ ਸੁਭਟ ਬਿਰੁੱਧੰ ਗਲਿਤ ਸੁਬੁੱਧੰ ਗਹਿ ਬਾਣੰ ॥
262.t: dhaayo kar kru'dha(n) subhaT biru'dha(n) galit subu'dha(n) geh baana(n) ||
262.e: That demon of vicious intellect, holding arrows in his hand and highly enraged marched forward to wage a war.

262.g: ਕੀਨੋ ਰਣ ਸੁੱਧੰ ਨਚਤ ਕਬੁੱਧੰ ਅਤ ਧੁਨ ਉੱਧੰ ਧਨੁ ਤਾਣੰ ॥
262.t: keeno ran su'dha(n) nachat kabu'dha(n) at dhun u'dha(n) dhan taana(n) ||
262.e: He fought a terrible war and amidst the pulled up bows in the battlefield, the headless trunks began to dance.

262.g: ਧਾਏ ਰਜਵਾਰੇ ਦੁੱਧਰ ਹਕਾਰੇ ਸੁ ਬ੍ਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ਕਰ ਕੋਪੰ ॥
262.t: dhaae rajavaare dhu'dhar hakaare su bran prahaare kar kopa(n) ||
262.e: The king moved forward while challenging and inflicting wounds on the warriors, they were in great ire

262.g: ਘਾਇਨ ਤਨ ਰੱਜੇ ਦੁ ਪਗ ਨ ਭੱਜੇ ਜਨੁ ਹਰ ਗੱਜੇ ਪਗ ਰੋਪੰ ॥੫੯੭॥
262.t: ghain tan ra'je dh pag na bha'je jan har ga'je pag ropa(n) ||597||
262.e: The wounds were inflicted on the bodies of the fighters, but still they are not fleeing and thundering like clouds, they are firmly standing and fighti
KALAS
With the increase of indignation the warriors attacked each other and
The armours and helmets were shattered,
The arrows were discharged from bows and
The bits of flesh fell on being chopped form the bodies of the enemies.598.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

262.g: ਸਾਇਕ ਜਣੁ ਛੂਟੇ ਤਿਮ ਅਰਿ ਜੂਟੇ ਬਖਤਰ ਫੂਟੇ ਜੇਬ ਜਿਰੇ ॥
262.t: saik jan chhooTe tim ar jooTe bakhatar fooTe jeb jire ||
262.e: As soon as the arrows are discharged, the enemies in still greather numbers gather and prepare to fight even with the shattered armour

262.g: ਮਸਹਰ ਭੁਖਿਆਏ ਤਿਮੁ ਅਰਿ ਧਾਏ ਸੱਸਤ੍ਰ ਨਚਾਇਨ ਫੇਰਿ ਫਿਰੇਾਂ ॥
262.t: masahar bhukhiaae tim ar dhaae sa'satr nachain fer fireaa(n) ||
262.e: They move forward and run like a hungry person here and there  they are roaming hither and thither, striking their weapons.

262.g: ਸਨਮੁਖਿ ਰਣ ਗਾਜੈਂ ਕਿਮਹੂੰ ਨ ਭਾਜੈਂ ਲਖ ਸੁਰ ਲਾਜੈਂ ਰਣ ਰੰਗੰ ॥
262.t: sanamukh ran gaajai(n) kimahoo(n) na bhaajai(n) lakh sur laajai(n) ran ra(n)ga(n) ||
262.e: They fight face to face and don not run away  seeing them waging war even the gods feel shy.

262.g: ਜੈ ਜੈ ਧੁਨ ਕਰਹੀ ਪੁਹਪਨ ਡਰਹੀ ਸੁ ਬਿਧਿ ਉਚਰਹੀ ਜੈ ਜੰਗੰ ॥੫੯੯॥
262.t: jai jai dhun karahee puhapan ddarahee su bidh ucharahee jai ja(n)ga(n) ||599||
262.e: The gods seeing the terrible war shower flowers with the sound of ‘hail, hail  they also hail the fight in the war arena.599.
KALAS
There is betel in the mouth of Ravana an the colour of his body is red, he is moving fearlessly in the battlefield
He has plastered his body with sandalwood
He is bright like the sun and is moving with a superior gait.600.
TRIBHANGI STANZA

263.g: ਤਨ ਸੁਭਤ ਸੁਰੰਗੰ ਛਬਿ ਅੰਗ ਅੰਗੰ ਲਜਤ ਅਨੰਗੰ ਲਖ ਨੈਣੰ ॥
263.t: tan subhat sura(n)ga(n) chhab a(n)g a(n)ga(n) lajat ana(n)ga(n) lakh naina(n) ||

263.g: ਸੋਭਿਤ ਕਚਕਾਰੇ ਅਤ ਘੁੰਘਰਾਰੇ ਰਸਨ ਰਸਾਰੇ ਮ੍ਰਿਦ ਬੈਣੰ ॥
263.t: sobhit kachakaare at ghu(n)gharaare rasan rasaare miradh baina(n) ||
263.e: Seeing his winsome body and elegant limbs, the god of love is feeling shy, he has back curly hair and sweet speech

263.g: ਮੁਖਿ ਛਕਤ ਸੁਬਾਸੰ ਦਿਨਸ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸੰ ਜਨੁ ਸਸ ਭਾਸੰ ਤਸ ਸੋਭੰ ॥
263.t: mukh chhakat subaasa(n) dhinas prakaasa(n) jan sas bhaasa(n) tas sobha(n) ||
263.e: His face is fragranted and appears shining like sun and glorifying like moon.

263.g: ਰੀਝਤ ਚਖ ਚਾਰੰ ਸੁਰਪੁਰ ਪਯਾਰੰ ਦੇਵ ਦਿਵਾਰੰ ਲਖਿ ਲੋਭੰ ॥੬੦੧॥
263.t: reejhat chakh chaara(n) surapur payaara(n) dhev dhivaara(n) lakh lobha(n) ||601||
263.e: On seeing him all feel delighted and the people of the abode of gods also do not hesitate to see him.601.

263.g: ਕਲਸ ॥
263.t: kalas ||
263.e: KALAS

263.g: ਚੰਦ੍ਰਹਾਸ ਏਕੰ ਕਰ ਧਾਰੀ ॥
263.t: cha(n)dhrahaas eka(n) kar dhaaree ||
263.e: In one of his hands there was the sword named Chandrahaas

263.g: ਦੁਤੀਆ ਧੋਪੁ ਗਹਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਤੀ ਕਟਾਰੀ ॥
263.t: dhuteeaa dhop geh tiratee kaTaaree ||
263.e: In the second hand was another arm named Dhop and in the third hand there was spear

263.g: ਚਤ੍ਰਥ ਹਾਥ ਸੈਹਥੀ ਉਜਿਆਰੀ ॥
263.t: chatrath haath saihathee ujiaaree ||
263.e: In his fourth hand there was a weapons named Saihathi having sharp glimmer,

263.g: ਗੋਫਨ ਗੁਰਜ ਕਰਤ ਚਮਕਾਰੀ ॥੬੦੨॥
263.t: gofan guraj karat chamakaaree ||602||
263.e: In his fifth hand and sixth hand there was a glittering mace and a weapon named Gophan.602.

263.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਭੰਗੀ ਛੰਦ ॥
263.t: tirabha(n)gee chha(n)dh ||
263.e: TRIBHANGI STANZA

263.g: ਸਤਏ ਅਸ ਭਾਰੀ ਗਦਹਿ ਉਭਾਰੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਸੂਲ ਸੁਧਾਰੀ ਛੁਰਕਾਰੀ ॥
263.t: sate as bhaaree gadheh ubhaaree tirasool sudhaaree chhurakaaree ||
263.e: In his seventh hand there was another heavy and swollen mace and

263.g: ਜੰਬੂਵਾ ਅਰ ਬਾਨੰ ਸੁ ਕਸਿ ਕਮਾਨੰ ਚਰਮ ਅਪ੍ਰਮਾਨੰ ਧਰ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
263.t: ja(n)boovaa ar baana(n) su kas kamaana(n) charam apramaana(n) dhar bhaaree ||
263.e: In other hands there were trident, pincers, arrows, bow etc. as weapons and arms.

263.g: ਪੰਦ੍ਰਏ ਗਲੋਲੰ ਪਾਸ ਅਮੋਲੰ ਪਰਸ ਅਡੋਲੰ ਹਥਿ ਨਾਲੰ ॥
263.t: pa(n)dhre galola(n) paas amola(n) paras addola(n) hath naala(n) ||
263.e: In his fifteenth hand there were an arm-like pellet bow and weapons named Pharsa.

263.g: ਬਿਛੂਆ ਪਹਰਾਯੰ ਪਟਾ ਭ੍ਰਮਾਯੰ ਜਿਮ ਜਮ ਧਾਯੰ ਬਿਕਰਾਲੰ ॥੬੦੩॥
263.t: bichhooaa paharaaya(n) paTaa bhramaaya(n) jim jam dhaaya(n) bikaraala(n) ||603||
263.e: He had worn in his hands steel-hooked weapons shaped like tiger’s claws and he was roaming like dreadful Yama.603.

263.g: ਕਲਸ ॥
263.t: kalas ||
263.e: KALAS

263.g: ਸਿਵ ਸਿਵ ਸਿਵ ਮੁਖ ਏਕ ਉਚਾਰੰ ॥
263.t: siv siv siv mukh ek uchaara(n) ||
263.e: He was repeating the name of Shiva from one face,

263.g: ਦੁਤੀਅ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਜਾਨਕੀ ਨਿਹਾਰੰ ॥
263.t: dhuteea prabhaa jaanakee nihaara(n) ||
263.e: From the second he was looking at the beauty of Sita

263.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਤੀਅ ਝੁੰਡ ਸਭ ਸੁਭਟ ਪਚਾਰੰ ॥
263.t: tirateea jhu(n)dd sabh subhaT pachaara(n) ||
263.e: From the third he was seeing his own warriors and

263.g: ਚਤ੍ਰਥ ਕਰਤ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰੰ ॥੬੦੪॥
263.t: chatrath karat maar hee maara(n) ||604||
263.e: From the fourth he was shouting “Kill, Kill”.604.

263.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਭੰਗੀ ਛੰਦ ॥
263.t: tirabha(n)gee chha(n)dh ||
263.e: TRIBHANGI STANZA

263.g: ਪਚਏ ਹਨਵੰਤੰ ਲਖ ਦੁਤ ਮੰਤੰ ਸੁ ਬਲ ਦੁਰੰਤੰ ਤਜਿ ਕਲਿਣੰ ॥
263.t: pache hanava(n)ta(n) lakh dhut ma(n)ta(n) su bal dhura(n)ta(n) taj kalina(n) ||

263.g: ਛਠਏ ਲਖਿ ਭ੍ਰਾਤੰ ਤਕਤ ਪਪਾਤੰ ਲਗਤ ਨ ਘਾਤੰ ਜੀਅ ਜਲਿਣੰ ॥
263.t: chhaThe lakh bhraata(n) takat papaata(n) lagat na ghaata(n) jeea jalina(n) ||
263.e: From his fifth face he was looking at Hanuman and repeating the mantra at great speed and was trying to pull his strength. From his sixth head he was seeing his fallen brother Kumbhkarn and his heart was burning.

263.g: ਸਤਏ ਲਖਿ ਰਘੁਪਤਿ ਕਪ ਦਲ ਅਧਪਤਿ ਸੁਭਟ ਬਿਕਟ ਮਤ ਜੁਤ ਭ੍ਰਾਤੰ ॥
263.t: sate lakh raghupat kap dhal adhapat subhaT bikaT mat jut bhraata(n) ||

263.g: ਅਠਿਓ ਸਿਰਿ ਢੋਰੈਂ ਨਵਮਿ ਨਿਹੋਰੈਂ ਦਸਯਨ ਬੋਰੈਂ ਰਿਸ ਰਾਤੰ ॥੬੦੫॥
263.t: aThio sir ddorai(n) navam nihorai(n) dhasayan borai(n) ris raata(n) ||605||
263.e: From his seventh head he was seeing Ram and the army of monkeys and other mighty warriors. He was shaking his eight head and surveying everything from his ninth head and he was getting highly infuriated with rage.605.

263.g: ਚੌਬੋਲਾ ਛੰਦ ॥
263.t: chauabolaa chha(n)dh ||
263.e: CHABOLA STANZA

263.g: ਧਾਏ ਮਹਾ ਬੀਰ ਸਾਧੇ ਸਿਤੰ ਤੀਰ ਕਾਛੇ ਰਣੰ ਚੀਰ ਬਾਨਾ ਸੁਹਾਏ ॥
263.t: dhaae mahaa beer saadhe sita(n) teer kaachhe rana(n) cheer baanaa suhaae ||
263.e: Settling their whit arrows the mighty warriors moved with beautiful dress on their bodies

263.g: ਰਵਾ ਕਰਦ ਮਰਕਬ ਯਲੋ ਤੇਜ ਇਮ ਸਭ ਚੂੰ ਤੁੰਦ ਅਜਦ ਹੋਓ ਮਿਆ ਜੰਗਾਹੇ ॥
263.t: ravaa karadh marakab yalo tej im sabh choo(n) tu(n)dh ajadh hoo miaa ja(n)gaahe ||
263.e: Their were very swift-moving and were exhibiting complete quickness in the battlefield

263.g: ਭਿੜੇ ਆਇ ਈਹਾ ਬੁਲੇ ਬੈਣ ਕੀਹਾ ਕਰੇਾਂ ਘਾਇ ਜੀਹਾ ਭਿੜੇ ਭੇੜ ਭੱਜੇ ॥
263.t: bhiRe aai ieehaa bule bain keehaa kareaa(n) ghai jeehaa bhiRe bheR bha'je ||
263.e: Sometimes they fight on this side and challenging on the other and whenever they strike the blows, the enemies flee

263.g: ਪੀਯੋ ਪੋਸਤਾਨੇ ਭਛੋ ਰਾਬੜੀਨੇ ਕਹਾ ਛੈਅਣੀ ਰੋਧਣੀਨੇ ਨਿਹਾਰੈਂ ॥੬੦੬॥
263.t: peeyo posataane bhachho raabaReene kahaa chhaianee rodhaneene nihaarai(n) ||606||
263.e: They appear like one intoxicated on eating hemp and roaming hither and thither.606.

263.g: ਗਾਜੇ ਮਹਾ ਸੂਰ ਘੁਮੀ ਰਣੰ ਹੂਰ ਭਰਮੀ ਨਭੰ ਪੂਰ ਬੇਖੰ ਅਨੂਪੰ ॥
263.t: gaaje mahaa soor ghumee rana(n) hoor bharamee nabha(n) poor bekha(n) anoopa(n) ||

263.g: ਵਲੇ ਵੱਲ ਸਾਈ ਜੀਵੀ ਜੁਗਾ ਤਾਈ ਤੈਂਡੇ ਘੋਲੀ ਜਾਈ ਅਲਾਵੀਤ ਐਸੇ ॥
263.t: vale va'l saiee jeevee jugaa taiee tai(n)dde gholee jaiee alaaveet aaise ||
263.e: The warriors roared and the heavenly damsels roamed in the sky in order to see the unique war. They prayed that this warrior waging the dreadful war should live for ages

263.g: ਲਗੋ ਲਾਰ ਥਾਨੇ ਬਰੋ ਰਾਜ ਮਾਨੇ ਕਹੋ ਅਉਰ ਕਾਨੇ ਹਠੀ ਛਾਡ ਥੇਸੋ ॥
263.t: lago laar thaane baro raaj maane kaho aaur kaane haThee chhaadd theso ||

263.g: ਬਰੋ ਆਨ ਮੋ ਕੋ ਭਜੋ ਆਨ ਤੋ ਕੋ ਚਲੋ ਦੇਵ ਲੋਕੋ ਤਜੋ ਬੇਗ ਲੰਕਾ ॥੬੦੭॥
263.t: baro aan mo ko bhajo aan to ko chalo dhev loko tajo beg la(n)kaa ||607||
263.e: And should firmly enjoy his rule. O warriors! forsake this Lanka and come to wed us and depart for heaven.607.

263.g: ਸ੍ਵੈਯਾ ॥
263.t: savaiyaa ||
263.e: SWAYYA

263.g: ਅਨੰਤਤੁਕਾ ॥
263.t: ana(n)tatukaa ||
263.e: (OF INNUMERABLE VERSES)

263.g: ਰੋਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਤਜ ਹੋਸ ਨਿਸਾਚਰ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਕੋ ਘਾਇ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
263.t: ros bharayo taj hos nisaachar sree raghuraaj ko ghai prahaare ||
263.e: Ravana, abandoning his senses, became very furious and attacked Ramchander,

263.g: ਜੋਸ ਬਡੋ ਕਰ ਕਉਸਲਿਸੰ ਅਧ ਬੀਚ ਹੀ ਤੇ ਸਰ ਕਾਟ ਉਤਾਰੇ ॥
263.t: jos baddo kar kausalisa(n) adh beech hee te sar kaaT utaare ||
263.e: The king of Raghu clan  on this side Ram intercepted midway his arrows

263.g: ਫੇਰ ਬਡੋ ਕਰ ਰੋਸ ਦਿਵਾਰਦਨ ਧਾਇ ਪਰੈਂ ਕਪਿ ਪੁੰਜ ਸੰਘਾਰੈ ॥
263.t: fer baddo kar ros dhivaaradhan dhai parai(n) kap pu(n)j sa(n)ghaarai ||

263.g: ਪੱਟਸ ਲੋਹ ਹਥੀ ਪਰ ਸੰਗੜੀਏ ਜੰਬੁਵੇ ਜਮਦਾੜ ਚਲਾਵੈ ॥੬੦੮॥
263.t: pa'Tas loh hathee par sa(n)gaRe'e ja(n)buve jamadhaaR chalaavai ||608||
263.e: Then he began to destroy collectively the army of monkeys and struck various types of terrible arms.608.

263.g: ਚੌਬੋਲਾ ਸ੍ਵੈਯਾ ॥
263.t: chauabolaa savaiyaa ||
263.e: CHABOLA SWAYYA

263.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਸਰਾਸਨ ਲੈ ਰਿਸ ਠਾਟ ਘਨੀ ਰਨ ਬਾਨ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
263.t: sree raghuraaj saraasan lai ris ThaaT ghanee ran baan prahaare ||

263.g: ਬੀਰਨ ਮਾਰ ਦੁਸਾਰ ਗਏ ਸਰ ਅੰਬਰ ਤੇ ਬਰਸੇ ਜਨ ਓਰੇ ॥
263.t: beeran maar dhusaar ge sar a(n)bar te barase jan ore ||
263.e: Ram took his bow in his hand and in great ire, discharged many arrows which killed the warriors and penetrating on the other side, came in shower again from the sky.

263.g: ਬਾਜ ਗਜੀ ਰਥ ਸਾਜ ਗਿਰੇ ਧਰ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਅਨੇਕ ਸੁ ਕਉਨ ਗਨਾਵੈ ॥
263.t: baaj gajee rath saaj gire dhar patr anek su kaun ganaavai ||

263.g: ਫਾਗਨ ਪਉਨ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡ ਬਹੇ ਬਨ ਪੱਤ੍ਰਨ ਤੇ ਜਨ ਪੱਤ੍ਰ ਉਡਾਨੇ ॥੬੦੯॥
263.t: faagan paun pracha(n)dd bahe ban pa'tran te jan pa'tr uddaane ||609||
263.e: Innumerable elephants, horses and chariots fell in the battlefield and it appeared that with the flow of the violent wind the leaves are seen flying.609.

263.g: ਸ੍ਵੈਯਾ ਛੰਦ ॥
263.t: savaiyaa chha(n)dh ||
263.e: SWAYYA STANZA

263.g: ਰੋਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਰਨ ਮੌ ਰਘੁਨਾਥ ਸੁ ਰਾਵਨ ਕੋ ਬਹੁ ਬਾਨ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
263.t: ros bharayo ran mau raghunaath su raavan ko bahu baan prahaare ||

263.g: ਸ੍ਰੋਣਨ ਨੈਕ ਲਗਯੋ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਤਨ ਫੋਰ ਜਿਰੈ ਤਨ ਪਾਰ ਪਧਾਰੇ ॥
263.t: sronan naik lagayo tin ke tan for jirai tan paar padhaare ||
263.e: On being enraged, Ram discharged many arrows on Ravana and those arrows saturated slightly with blood, penetrated through the body to the other side

263.g: ਬਾਜ ਗਜੀ ਰਥ ਰਾਜ ਰਥੀ ਰਣ ਭੂਮਿ ਗਿਰੇ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਸੰਘਾਰੇ ॥
263.t: baaj gajee rath raaj rathee ran bhoom gire ieh bhaat sa(n)ghaare ||

264.g: ਜਾਨੋ ਬਸੰਤ ਕੇ ਅੰਤ ਸਮੈ ਕਦਲੀ ਦਲ ਪਉਨ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡ ਉਖਾਰੇ ॥੬੧੦॥
264.t: jaano basa(n)t ke a(n)t samai kadhalee dhal paun pracha(n)dd ukhaare ||610||
264.e: The elephants, horses, chariots and charioteers fell down in the battlefield after having been chopped like the trees of banana uprooted and thrown around by the violent wind at the end of spring.610.

264.g: ਧਾਇ ਪਰੇ ਕਰ ਕੋਪ ਬਨੇਚਰ ਹੈ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਜੀਅ ਰੋਸ ਜਗਯੋ ॥
264.t: dhai pare kar kop banechar hai tin ke jeea ros jagayo ||

264.g: ਕਿਲਕਾਰ ਪੁਕਾਰ ਪਰੇ ਚਹੂੰ ਘਾਰਣ ਛਾਡਿ ਹਠੀ ਨਹਿ ਏਕ ਭਗਯੋ ॥
264.t: kilakaar pukaar pare chahoo(n) ghaaran chhaadd haThee neh ek bhagayo ||
264.e: The forces of monkeys also fell on the enemy, having been greatly enraged in the heart and gushed forward from all the four sides, shouting violently without retreating form its position.

264.g: ਗਹਿ ਬਾਨ ਕਮਾਨ ਗਦਾ ਬਰਛੀ ਉਤ ਤੇ ਦਲ ਰਾਵਨ ਕੋ ਉਮਗਯੋ ॥
264.t: geh baan kamaan gadhaa barachhee ut te dhal raavan ko umagayo ||

264.g: ਭਟ ਜੂਝਿ ਅਰੂਝਿ ਗਿਰੇ ਧਰਣੀ ਦਿਜਰਾਜ ਭ੍ਰਮਯੋ ਸਿਵ ਧਯਾਨ ਡਿਗਯੋ ॥੬੧੧॥
264.t: bhaT joojh aroojh gire dharanee dhijaraaj bhramayo siv dhayaan ddigayo ||611||
264.e: From the other side, the army of Ravana rushed forward taking its weapons and arms like arrows, bows, maces, fell in such a way that the moon taking its course got illusioned and the contemplation of Shiva was obstructed.611.

264.g: ਜੂਝਿ ਅਰੂਝਿ ਗਿਰੇ ਭਟਵਾ ਤਨ ਘਾਇਨ ਘਾਇ ਘਨੇ ਭਿਭਰਾਨੇ ॥
264.t: joojh aroojh gire bhaTavaa tan ghain ghai ghane bhibharaane ||

264.g: ਜੰਬੁਕ ਗਿੱਧ ਪਿਸਾਚ ਨਿਸਾਚਰ ਫੂਲ ਫਿਰੇ ਰਨ ਮੌ ਰਹਸਾਨੇ ॥
264.t: ja(n)buk gi'dh pisaach nisaachar fool fire ran mau rahasaane ||
264.e: After receiving wounds on the body, the warriors swung and began to fall and the jackals, vultures, ghosts and fiends were delighted in mind.

264.g: ਕਾਪ ਉਠੀ ਸੁ ਦਿਸਾ ਬਿਦਿਸਾ ਦਿਗਪਾਲਨ ਫੇਰ ਪ੍ਰਲੈ ਅਨੁਮਾਨੇ ॥
264.t: kaap uThee su dhisaa bidhisaa dhigapaalan fer pralai anumaane ||
264.e: All the directions trembled on seeing the terrible war and the digpals (supervisors and directors) guessed the arrival of doomsday

264.g: ਭੂਮਿ ਅਕਾਸ ਉਦਾਸ ਭਏ ਗਨ ਦੇਵ ਅਦੇਵ ਭ੍ਰਮੇ ਭਹਰਾਨੇ ॥੬੧੨॥
264.t: bhoom akaas udhaas bhe gan dhev adhev bhrame bhaharaane ||612||
264.e: The earth and sky became anxious and seeing the dreadfulness of the war the gods and demons were both bewildered.612.

264.g: ਰਾਵਨ ਰੋਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਰਨ ਮੋ ਰਿਸ ਸੌ ਸਰ ਓਘ ਪ੍ਰਓਘ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
264.t: raavan ros bharayo ran mo ris sau sar ogh progh prahaare ||
264.e: Being highly infuriated in mind Ravana began to discharge arrows collectively and

264.g: ਭੂਮਿ ਅਕਾਸ ਦਿਸਾ ਬਿਦਿਸਾ ਸਭ ਓਰ ਰੁਕੇ ਨਹਿ ਜਾਤ ਨਿਹਾਰੇ ॥
264.t: bhoom akaas dhisaa bidhisaa sabh or ruke neh jaat nihaare ||
264.e: With his arrows the earth, sky and all directions were torn asunder

264.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਸਰਾਸਨ ਲੈ ਛਿਨ ਮੌ ਛੁਭ ਕੈ ਸਰ ਪੁੰਜ ਨਿਵਾਰੇ ॥
264.t: sree raghuraaj saraasan lai chhin mau chhubh kai sar pu(n)j nivaare ||
264.e: On this side Ram was enraged for and instant and destroyed the collective discharging of all those arrows and

264.g: ਜਾਨਕ ਭਾਨ ਉਦੈ ਨਿਸ ਕਉ ਲਖਿ ਕੈ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਤਪ ਤੇਜ ਪਧਾਰੇ ॥੬੧੩॥
264.t: jaanak bhaan udhai nis kau lakh kai sabh hee tap tej padhaare ||613||
264.e: The darkness that had spread on account of arrows, got cleared by the spread of the sunshine again on all the four sides.613.

264.g: ਰੋਸ ਭਰੇ ਰਨ ਮੋ ਰਘੁਨਾਥ ਕਮਾਨ ਲੈ ਬਾਨ ਅਨੇਕ ਚਲਾਏ ॥
264.t: ros bhare ran mo raghunaath kamaan lai baan anek chalaae ||
264.e: Filled with anger Ram discharged many arrows and

264.g: ਬਾਜ ਗਜੀ ਗਜਰਾਜ ਘਨੇ ਰਥ ਰਾਜ ਬਨੇ ਕਰਿ ਰੋਸ ਉਡਾਏ ॥
264.t: baaj gajee gajaraaj ghane rath raaj bane kar ros uddaae ||
264.e: Caused the elephants, horses and charioteers to fly away

264.g: ਜੇ ਦੁਖ ਦੇਹ ਕਟੇ ਸੀਅ ਕੇ ਹਿਤ ਤੇ ਰਨ ਆਜ ਪ੍ਰਤੱਖ ਦਿਖਾਏ ॥
264.t: je dhukh dheh kaTe seea ke hit te ran aaj prata'kh dhikhaae ||
264.e: The way in which the anguish of Sita could be removed and she could be set free,

264.g: ਰਾਜੀਵ ਲੋਚਨ ਰਾਮ ਕੁਮਾਰ ਘਨੋ ਰਨ ਘਾਲ ਘਨੋ ਘਰ ਘਾਏ ॥੬੧੪॥
264.t: raajeev lochan raam kumaar ghano ran ghaal ghano ghar ghaae ||614||
264.e: Ram made today all such efforts and that lotus-eyed one caused the desertion of many homes with his terrible warfare.614.

264.g: ਰਾਵਨ ਰੋਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਗਰਜਯੋ ਰਨ ਮੋ ਲਹਿ ਕੈ ਸਭ ਸੈਨ ਭਜਾਨਯੋ ॥
264.t: raavan ros bharayo garajayo ran mo leh kai sabh sain bhajaanayo ||
264.e: Ravana thundered in rage and causing his army to rush forward,

264.g: ਆਪ ਹੀ ਹਾਕ ਹਥਿਯਾਰ ਹਠੀ ਗਹਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਨੰਦਨ ਸੋ ਰਣ ਠਾਨਯੋ ॥
264.t: aap hee haak hathiyaar haThee geh sree raghuna(n)dhan so ran Thaanayo ||
264.e: Shouting loudly and holding his weapons in his hands, he came straight towards Ram and fought with him

264.g: ਚਾਬਕ ਮਾਰ ਕੁਦਾਇ ਤੁਰੰਗਨ ਜਾਇ ਪਰਯੋ ਕਛੁ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਨ ਮਾਨਯੋ ॥
264.t: chaabak maar kudhai tura(n)gan jai parayo kachh traas na maanayo ||
264.e: He caused his horses to gallop fearlessly by whipping them.

264.g: ਬਾਨਨ ਤੇ ਬਿਧੁ ਬਾਹਨ ਤੇ ਮਨ ਮਾਰਤ ਕੋ ਰਥ ਛੋਰਿ ਸਿਧਾਨਯੋ ॥੬੧੫॥
264.t: baanan te bidh baahan te man maarat ko rath chhor sidhaanayo ||615||
264.e: He left his chariot I order to kill Ram with his arrows and came forward.615.

264.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਨੰਦਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਜ ਕੇ ਜਬ ਛੋਰ ਸਰਾਸਨ ਬਾਨ ਉਡਾਨੇ ॥
264.t: sree raghuna(n)dhan kee bhuj ke jab chhor saraasan baan uddaane ||
264.e: When the arrows were discharged form the hands of Ram the earth,

264.g: ਭੂੰਮਿ ਅਕਾਸ ਪਤਾਰ ਚਹੂੰ ਚਕ ਪੂਰ ਰਹੇ ਨਹੀ ਜਾਤ ਪਛਾਨੇ ॥
264.t: bhoo(n)m akaas pataar chahoo(n) chak poor rahe nahee jaat pachhaane ||
264.e: Sky, netherworld and four directions could hardly be recognized

264.g: ਤੋਰ ਸਨਾਹ ਸੁਬਾਹਨ ਕੇ ਤਨ ਆਹ ਕਰੀ ਨਹੀ ਪਾਰ ਪਰਾਨੇ ॥
264.t: tor sanaeh subaahan ke tan aaeh karee nahee paar paraane ||
264.e: Those arrows, piercing through the armours of warriors and killing them without the utterance of a sigh,

265.g: ਛੋਦ ਕਰੋਟਨ ਓਟਨ ਕੋਟ ਅਟਾਨਮੋ ਜਾਨਕੀ ਬਾਨ ਪਛਾਨੇ ॥੬੧੬॥
265.t: chhodh karoTan oTan koT aTaanamo jaanakee baan pachhaane ||616||
265.e: They penetrated to the other side, when the arrows fell after piercing the steel-armours, Sita realized that these arrows were discharged by Ram.616.

265.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਸੁਰਾਰਦਨ ਕੇ ਕਰ ਕੋ ਜਿਨ ਏਕ ਹੀ ਬਾਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤਨ ਚਾਖਯੋ ॥
265.t: sree asuraaradhan ke kar ko jin ek hee baan bikhai tan chaakhayo ||

265.g: ਭਾਜ ਸਰਯੋ ਨ ਭਿਰਯੋ ਹਠ ਕੈ ਭਟ ਏਕ ਹੀ ਘਾਇ ਧਰਾ ਪਰ ਰਾਖਯੋ ॥
265.t: bhaaj sarayo na bhirayo haTh kai bhaT ek hee ghai dharaa par raakhayo ||
265.e: He, who was struck by arrows of Ram, that warrior could neither run away from that place nor could fight but fell dead on the ground.

265.g: ਛੇਦ ਸਨਾਹ ਸੁਬਾਹਨ ਕੋ ਸਰ ਓਟਨ ਕੋਟ ਕਰੋਟਨ ਨਾਖਯੋ ॥
265.t: chhedh sanaeh subaahan ko sar oTan koT karoTan naakhayo ||

265.g: ਸੁਆਰ ਜੁਝਾਰ ਅਪਾਰ ਹਠੀ ਰਨ ਹਾਰ ਗਿਰੇ ਧਰ ਹਾਇ ਨ ਭਾਖਯੋ ॥੬੧੭॥
265.t: suaar jujhaar apaar haThee ran haar gire dhar hai na bhaakhayo ||617||
265.e: The arrows of Ram pierced through the armour of warriors and then mighty fighters fell down on the earth without uttering a sign.617.

265.g: ਆਨ ਅਰੇ ਸੁ ਮਰੇ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਭਟ ਜੀਤ ਬਚੇ ਰਨ ਛਾਡਿ ਪਰਾਨੇ ॥
265.t: aan are su mare sabh hee bhaT jeet bache ran chhaadd paraane ||
265.e: Ravana called all his warriors, but those remaining fighters fled away

265.g: ਦੇਵ ਅਦੇਵਨ ਕੇ ਜਿਤੀਯਾ ਰਨ ਕੋਟ ਹਤੇ ਕਰ ਏਕ ਨ ਜਾਨੇ ॥
265.t: dhev adhevan ke jiteeyaa ran koT hate kar ek na jaane ||
265.e: Ravna killed millions of gods and demons, but it made no difference in the battlefield.

265.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਪ੍ਰਾਕ੍ਰਮ ਕੋ ਲਖ ਤੇਜ ਸੰਬੂਹ ਸਭੈ ਭਹਰਾਨੇ ॥
265.t: sree raghuraaj praakram ko lakh tej sa(n)booh sabhai bhaharaane ||
265.e: Seeing the power of Ram the illustrious persons were perturbed and

265.g: ਓਟਨ ਕੂਦ ਕਰੋਟਨ ਫਾਧ ਸੁ ਲੰਕਹਿ ਛਾਡਿ ਬਿਲੰਕ ਸਿਧਾਨੇ ॥੬੧੮॥
265.t: oTan koodh karoTan faadh su la(n)keh chhaadd bila(n)k sidhaane ||618||
265.e: Jumping over the walls of the citadel, they ran away.618.

265.g: ਰਾਵਨ ਰੋਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਰਨ ਮੋ ਗਹਿ ਬੀਸ ਹੂੰ ਬਾਹਿ ਹਥਯਾਰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
265.t: raavan ros bharayo ran mo geh bees hoo(n) baeh hathayaar prahaare ||

265.g: ਭੂੰਮਿ ਅਕਾਸ ਦਿਸਾ ਬਿਦਿਸਾ ਚਕਿ ਚਾਰ ਰੁਕੇ ਨਹੀ ਜਾਤ ਨਿਹਾਰੇ ॥
265.t: bhoo(n)m akaas dhisaa bidhisaa chak chaar ruke nahee jaat nihaare ||
265.e: In great fury Ravana attacked with weapons from all the twenty arms and with his blows the earth, sky and all the four directions became invisible

265.g: ਫੋਕਨ ਤੈ ਫਲ ਤੈ ਮੱਧ ਤੈ ਅਧ ਤੈ ਬਧ ਕੈ ਰਣ ਮੰਡਲ ਡਾਰੇ ॥
265.t: fokan tai fal tai ma'dh tai adh tai badh kai ran ma(n)ddal ddaare ||

265.g: ਛੰਤ੍ਰ ਧੁਜਾ ਬਰ ਬਾਜ ਰਥੀ ਰਥ ਕਾਟਿ ਸਭੈ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਉਤਾਰੇ ॥੬੧੯॥
265.t: chha(n)tr dhujaa bar baaj rathee rath kaaT sabhai raghuraaj utaare ||619||
265.e: Ram threw away the enemies from the war-arena, chopping them easily like a fruit. Ram chopped and threw all the canopies, banners, horses and charioteers belonging to Ravana.619.

265.g: ਰਾਵਨ ਚਉਪ ਚਲਯੋ ਚਪ ਕੈ ਨਿਜ ਬਾਜ ਬਿਹੀਨ ਜਬੈ ਰਥ ਜਾਨਯੋ ॥
265.t: raavan chaup chalayo chap kai nij baaj biheen jabai rath jaanayo ||

265.g: ਢਾਲ ਤ੍ਰਿਸੂਲ ਗਦਾ ਬਰਛੀ ਗਹਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਨੰਦਨ ਸੋ ਰਨ ਠਾਨਯੋ ॥
265.t: ddaal tirasool gadhaa barachhee geh sree raghuna(n)dhan so ran Thaanayo ||
265.e: When Ravana saw his chariot deprived of the horses, he marched forward quickly and holding his shield, trident mace and spear in his hands he fought with Ram.

265.g: ਧਾਇ ਪਰਯੋ ਲਲਕਾਰ ਹਠੀ ਕਪ ਪੁੰਜਨ ਕੋ ਕਛੁ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਨ ਮਾਨਯੋ ॥
265.t: dhai parayo lalakaar haThee kap pu(n)jan ko kachh traas na maanayo ||
265.e: The persistent Ravana, without any fear of the forces of the monkeys

265.g: ਅੰਗਦ ਆਦਿ ਹਨਵੰਤ ਤੇ ਲੈ ਭਟ ਕੋਟ ਹੁਤੇ ਕਰ ਏਕ ਨ ਜਾਨਯੋ ॥੬੨੦॥
265.t: a(n)gadh aadh hanava(n)t te lai bhaT koT hute kar ek na jaanayo ||620||
265.e: Moved forward fearlessly, shouting violently. There were many warriors those like Angad, Hanuman etc., but he did not fear anyone.620.

265.g: ਰਾਵਨ ਕੋ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਜਬੈ ਰਣ ਮੰਡਲ ਆਵਤ ਮੱਧਿ ਨਿਹਾਰਯੋ ॥
265.t: raavan ko raghuraaj jabai ran ma(n)ddal aavat ma'dh nihaarayo ||

265.g: ਬੀਸ ਸਿਲਾ ਸਿਤ ਸਾਇਕ ਲੈ ਕਰਿ ਕੋਪੁ ਬਡੋ ਉਰ ਮੱਧ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰਯੋ ॥
265.t: bees silaa sit saik lai kar kop baddo ur ma'dh prahaarayo ||
265.e: When the king of Raghava clan saw Ravna coming forward, he (Ram) attacked him by discharging his twenty arrows like slabs on his chest.

265.g: ਭੇਦ ਚਲੇ ਮਰਮ ਸੱਥਲ ਕੋ ਸਰ ਸ੍ਰੋਣ ਨਦੀ ਸਰ ਬੀਚ ਪਖਾਰਯੋ ॥
265.t: bhedh chale maram sa'thal ko sar sron nadhee sar beech pakhaarayo ||

265.g: ਆਗੇ ਹੀ ਰੇਾਂਗ ਚਲਯੋ ਹਠਿ ਕੈ ਭਟ ਧਾਮ ਕੋ ਭੂਲ ਨ ਨਾਮ ਉਚਾਰਯੋ ॥੬੨੧॥
265.t: aage hee reaa(n)g chalayo haTh kai bhaT dhaam ko bhool na naam uchaarayo ||621||
265.e: These arrows penetrated through his vital parts and he bathed in the stream of blood. Ravana fell down and crawled forward, he forgot even the location of his house.621.

265.g: ਰੋਸ ਭਰਯੋ ਰਨ ਮੌ ਰਘੁਨਾਥ ਸੁ ਪਾਨ ਕੇ ਬੀਚ ਸਰਾਸਨ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥
265.t: ros bharayo ran mau raghunaath su paan ke beech saraasan lai kai ||

265.g: ਪਾਚਕ ਪਾਇ ਹਟਾਇ ਦਯੋ ਤਿਹ ਬੀਸਹੂੰ ਬਾਹਿ ਬਿਨਾ ਓਹ ਕੈ ਕੈ ॥
265.t: paachak pai haTai dhayo teh beesahoo(n) baeh binaa oh kai kai ||
265.e: Ram, the king of Raghava clan, in great fury, taking his bow in his hand and taking five steps backward, chopped all his twenty arms

265.g: ਦੈ ਦਸ ਬਾਨ ਬਿਮਾਨ ਦਸੋ ਸਿਰ ਕਾਟ ਦਏ ਸਿਵ ਲੋਕ ਪਠੈ ਕੈ ॥
265.t: dhai dhas baan bimaan dhaso sir kaaT dhe siv lok paThai kai ||
265.e: With ten arrows be chopped his ten heads for dispatching them to the abode of Shiva

265.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਬਰਯੋ ਸੀਅ ਕੋ ਬਹੁਰੋ ਜਨੁ ਜੁੱਧ ਸੁਯੰਬਰ ਜੈ ਕੈ ॥੬੨੨॥
265.t: sree raghuraaj barayo seea ko bahuro jan ju'dh suya(n)bar jai kai ||622||
265.e: After the war Ram wedded Sita again as if he had conquered her in the ceremony of Swayyamvara.622.

265.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਰਾਮਵਤਾਰ ਦਸ ਸਿਰ ਬਧਹ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ॥
265.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake raamavataar dhas sir badheh dhiaai samaapatam sat ||
265.e: End of the chapter entitled ‘Killing of the Ten-headed (Ravana) in Ramavtar in BACHITTAR NATAK.

265.g: ਅਥ ਮਦੋਦਰੀ ਸਮੋਧ ਬਭੀਛਨ ਕੋ ਲੰਕ ਰਾਜ ਦੀਬੋ ॥
265.t: ath madhodharee samodh babheechhan ko la(n)k raaj dheebo ||
265.e: Now begins the description of contemporaneous knowledge to Mandodari and the bestowal of the kingdom of Lanka to Vibhishana:

265.g: ਸੀਤਾ ਮਿਲਬੋ ਕਥਨੰ ॥
265.t: seetaa milabo kathana(n) ||
265.e: Description of the Union with Sita :

265.g: ਸ੍ਵੈਯਾ ਛੰਦ ॥
265.t: savaiyaa chha(n)dh ||
265.e: SWAYYA STANZA

265.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਡਰਾਕੁਲ ਥੋ ਜਿੱਹ ਕੇ ਡਰ ਸੂਰਜ ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਹੁਤੋ ਭਯ ਭੀਤੋ ॥
265.t: ei(n)dhr ddaraakul tho ji'h ke ddar sooraj cha(n)dhr huto bhay bheeto ||

265.g: ਲੂਟ ਲਯੋ ਧਨ ਜਉਨ ਧਨੇਸ ਕੋ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਹੁਤੋ ਚਿਤ ਮੋਨਨਿ ਚੀਤੋ ॥
265.t: looT layo dhan jaun dhanes ko braham huto chit monan cheeto ||
265.e: He, from whom Indra, moon and sun felt baffled, he who had plundered the stores of Kuber and he before whom Brahma kept silent

265.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਸੇ ਭੂਪ ਅਨੇਕ ਲਰੈ ਇਨ ਸੌ ਫਿਰਿ ਕੈ ਗ੍ਰਹ ਜਾਤ ਨ ਜੀਤੋ ॥
265.t: ei(n)dhr se bhoop anek larai in sau fir kai greh jaat na jeeto ||
265.e: He with whom many beings like Indra fought, but who could not be conquered

265.g: ਸੋ ਰਨ ਆਜ ਭਲੈਂ ਰਘੁਰਾਜ ਸੁ ਜੁੱਧ ਸੁਯੰਬਰ ਕੈ ਸੀਅ ਜੀਤੋ ॥੬੨੩॥
265.t: so ran aaj bhalai(n) raghuraaj su ju'dh suya(n)bar kai seea jeeto ||623||
265.e: Conquering him today in the battlefield, Ram also conquered Sita as in the ceremony of Svayyamvara.623.

265.g: ਅਲਕਾ ਛੰਦ ॥
265.t: alakaa chha(n)dh ||
265.e: ALKA STANZA

265.g: ਚਟਪਟ ਸੈਣੰ ਖਟਪਟ ਭਾਜੇ ॥
265.t: chaTapaT saina(n) khaTapaT bhaaje ||

265.g: ਝਟਪਟ ਜੁੱਝਯੋ ਲਖ ਰਣ ਰਾਜੇ ॥
265.t: jhaTapaT ju'jhayo lakh ran raaje ||
265.e: The forces ran quickly and began to fight, the warriors ran speedily and

265.g: ਸਟਪਟ ਭਾਜੇ ਅਟਪਟ ਸੂਰੰ ॥
265.t: saTapaT bhaaje aTapaT soora(n) ||

265.g: ਝਟਪਟ ਬਿਸਰੀ ਘਟ ਪਟ ਹੂਰੰ ॥੬੨੪॥
265.t: jhaTapaT bisaree ghaT paT hoora(n) ||624||
265.e: They forgot their thoughts about the heavenly damsels.624.

265.g: ਚਟਪਟ ਪੈਠੇ ਖਟਪਟ ਲੰਕੰ ॥
265.t: chaTapaT paiThe khaTapaT la(n)ka(n) ||

265.g: ਰਣ ਤਜ ਸੂਰੰ ਸਰ ਧਰ ਬੰਕੰ ॥
265.t: ran taj soora(n) sar dhar ba(n)ka(n) ||
265.e: The warriors abandoning the field and the arrows entered Lanka

265.g: ਝਲਹਲ ਬਾਰੰ ਨਰਬਰ ਨੈਣੰ ॥
265.t: jhalahal baara(n) narabar naina(n) ||

265.g: ਧਕਿ ਧਕਿ ਉਚਰੇ ਭਕਿ ਭਕਿ ਬੈਣੰ ॥੬੨੫॥
265.t: dhak dhak uchare bhak bhak baina(n) ||625||
265.e: Seeing Ram with their own eyes they raised utterances of lamentation.625.

265.g: ਨਰ ਬਰ ਰਾਮੰ ਬਰਨਰ ਮਾਰੋ ॥
265.t: nar bar raama(n) baranar maaro ||

265.g: ਝਟਪਟ ਬਾਹੰ ਕਟਿ ਕਟਿ ਡਾਰੋ ॥
265.t: jhaTapaT baaha(n) kaT kaT ddaaro ||
265.e: The superb Ram killed all of them and chopped their arms

265.g: ਤਬ ਸਭ ਭਾਜੇ ਰਖ ਰਖ ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ ॥
265.t: tab sabh bhaaje rakh rakh praana(n) ||

265.g: ਖਟਪਟ ਮਾਰੇ ਝਟਪਟ ਬਾਣੰ ॥੬੨੬॥
265.t: khaTapaT maare jhaTapaT baana(n) ||626||
265.e: Then all (others) saving themselves, fled away and Ram showered arrows on those running fighters.626.

265.g: ਚਟਪਟ ਰਾਨੀ ਸਟਪਟ ਧਾਈ ॥
265.t: chaTapaT raanee saTapaT dhaiee ||

265.g: ਰਟਪਟ ਰੋਵਤ ਅਟਪਟ ਆਈ ॥
265.t: raTapaT rovat aTapaT aaiee ||
265.e: All the queen ran weeping instantly and came to fall at the feet of Ram

266.e: Ram saw all the spectacle.627.
The queens rolled on the earth and began to weep and lament in various ways

266.g: ਬਟ ਹਰਿ ਕੂਕੈਂ ਨਟ ਵਰ ਭੇਸੰ ॥੬੨੮॥
266.t: baT har kookai(n) naT var bhesa(n) ||628||
266.e: They pulled their hair and garments and cried and shrieked in various ways.628.
They began to tear their raiments and put the dust on their heads
They in great sorrow cried, threw themselves down and rolled.629.
RASAAVAL STANZA
When all of them saw the most beautiful Ram, they bowed their heads and stood before him.630.
They were allured to see the beauty of Ram
There was talk about Ram on all the four sides and they all gave Ram the kingdom of Lanka like the tax-payer setting tax with the authority.631.
Ram bowed down his eyes filled with grace
Seeing him, the tears of joy flowed down from the eyes of people like the rain falling from the clouds.632.
The woman allured by lust, were delighted to see Ram and they all ended their identity in Ram, the abode of Dharma. 633.
They all absorbed their minds in Ram, forsaking the love of their husbands and looking towards him resolutely, they began to talk with one another.634.
Ram, the Lord of Sita, is winsome and abductor of the mind
He is stealing the conscious mind like a thief.635.
All the wives of Ravana were told to abandon the sorrow of their husband and touch the feet of Ram
All of them came forward and fell on his feet.636.
The most beautiful Ram recognized their feelings
He absorbed himself in the minds of all and all of them pursued him like shadow.637.
Ram appeared to them in golden hue and looked like king of all kings
The eyes of all were dyed in his love and the gods were delighted to see him from the sky.638.

267.e: He, who saw Ram even once, she was completely allured.639.
She forgot the consciousness of all else seeing the beauty of Ram and began to talk to supremely mighty Ram.640.
The speech of Ram addressed to Mandodari :
“O queen! I have not committed a mistake in killing your husband, think rightly in your mind about it and the blame me.641.
“I should get my Sita back, so that the work of righteousness may move forward
” (Saying in this way) Ram sent Hanuman, she son of wind-god, like an envoy (in advance).642.
Searching for Sita, he reached there, where she was sitting in the garden under a tree.643.

268.e: Hanuman, falling at the feet of Sita, said, “O mother Sita! Ram has killed the enemy (Ravana) and now he is standing at your door.644.
“O mother Sita! go to the place of Ram quickly, where he has won and lightened the burden of the earth by killing all the enemie.”645.
Being highly pleased Sita accompanied Hanuman, she saw Ram and found Ram retaining his precious beauty.646.
Sita fell at the feet of Ram who saw towards her and addressed to that lady of lotus eyes and sweet speech 647
“O Sita! enter the fire, so that you may become pure.” She agreed and prepared a pyre of fire.648.
She merged in the fire like the lightning seen in the clouds
She became one with fire like Gita with Shrutis (recorded texts).649.
She entered the fire and came out like pure gold
Ram hold her to his bosom and the poets sang in praise about this fact.650.
All the saints accepted this type of fire-test and the beings of the three worlds accepted this fact
The musical instruments of victory were played and Ram also thundered in great joy.651.
The pure SIta was conquered like a superbly auspicious song
All the gods began to shower flowers from the sky.652.

268.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਰਾਮਵਤਾਰ ਬਭੀਛਨ ਕੋ ਲੰਕਾ ਕੋ ਰਾਜ ਦੀਬੋ ਮਦੋਦਰੀ ਸਮੋਧ ਕੀਬੋ ਸੀਤਾ ਮਿਲਬੋ ਧਯਾਇ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥੧੮॥
268.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake raamavataar babheechhan ko la(n)kaa ko raaj dheebo madhodharee samodh keebo seetaa milabo dhayai samaapata(n) ||18||
268.e: End of the chapter entitled The Bestowal of Kingdom on Vibhishan, Imparting of Contemporaneous Knowledge to Mandodari and the Union with Sita’ in Ramavtar in BACHITTAR NATAK.
Now begins the description of the entry into Ayodhya :
RASAAVAL STANZA
Gaining victory in war, then Ram mounted on the air-vehicle Pushpak
All the warriors roared in great joy and the musical instruments of victory resounded.653.
The monkeys in great delight caused the air-vehicle to fly and they saw Avadhpuri, beautiful like heaven.654.
MAKRA STANZA
Ram has come and brought Sita with him and

269.e: There are rejoicings in the city  the joy is growing in the heart of Avadh.655.
The women are coming at speed, there is endless crowd, all are standing amazed and asking, “Where is our Lord Ram?”656.
“He, whose hair are unique and black like serpents
He whose thinking is wonderful, where is that dear Ram?657.
“He who is ever in blossom like garden and ever thoughtful about his kingdom
He, who hath stolen our mind, where is that Ram.658.
“He, who hath stolen our heart and given as separation from him, were is that flower-faced and alluring Ram?659.
“Someone may tell us and take whatever he wants from us, but he should tell us where is that alluring Ram?660.
“He accepted the orders of his father like a drunkard accepting every word of the giver of intoxicant and he left his country. Where is he, the beauty-incarnation of the world and rose-faced?661.
“The wagtail (birds) were envious of his cruel gestures, he who hath allured our mind, where is that Ram of blossomed face?662.
“His gestures were the gestures of an intoxicated person
All the world is obedient to his personality  someone may tell where is that flower-faced Ram?663.
“The splendour of this face was significant and he was perfect in intellect
He, who is a vessel full of the wine of heart’s love, where is that flower faced Ram?664.
“After conquering the tyrants the beloved Ram has come back from distant lands
Where is he, the perfect one in all arts and who hath flower-like face?665.
“His qualities are known all over the world and he is famous in the seven regions of the world
He whose light hath spread throughout the world, where is that flower-faced Ram?666.
“He who conquered the tyrants with the blows of his arrows

270.e: Where is he who mouth the air-vehicle Pushapak and accompanies Sita?667.
“He who sacrificed thousands of his joys in order to please his mother, where is he? The mother Sita may also be congratulate today, but someone may tell us where is that flower-faced Ram?”668.

270.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਰਾਮ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਸੀਤਾ ਅਯੁਧਿਆ ਆਗਮ ਨਾਮ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤੰ ॥
270.t: eit sree raam avataar seetaa ayudhiaa aagam naam dhiaai samaapata(n) ||
270.e: End of the chapter entitled ‘The Entry of Sita in Ayodhya’ in Ramvatar.
Now begins the description of the Meeting with the Mother :
When the people heard that Ram had returned, then all the people ran and fell at his feet
Someone swung she fly-whisk, someone offered the betel
Ram fell at the feet of his mother and his mothers hugged him to their bosom.670.
On being hugged he was weeping in order to wash away all his suffering
The brave Ram began to talk and all the mothers listened.671.
Then he met the mother of Lakshman and the brother Bharat and Shatrughan touched his feet. On account of the joy of union, unaccountable charity was given.672.

271.e: Then Ram met the mother of Bharat and told her all that happened with him
Ram said, “O mother, I am thankful to you because you have made me free from indebtedness.673.
“You are not to be blamed for this, because it was recorded in my destiny, whatever happens, has to happen, none can describe it.”674.
He pacified his mother in this way and then he met his brother Bharat. Bharat on hearing his arrival ran towards him and touched his head with the feet of Ram.675.
Ram hugged him to his bosom and cleared all the doubts
Then he met Shatrugan, who had expert knowledge of weapons and Shastras.676.
The brothers cleansed the dust from the feet and matted hair of Ram. They worlshipped him in royal way and the Brahmins recited the Vedas.677.
All the brothers sang full of love. Ram was made the king and all the works were completed in this way.678.
The Brahmins were called in and with the recitation of Vedic mantras Ram was enthroned
On all the four sides resounded the musical instruments denoting victory.679.

271.g: ਧਰੇ ਅੱਤ੍ਰ ਨੀਕੇ ਪੁਰੀ ਅਉਧ ਆਏ ॥
271.t: dhare a'tr neeke puree aaudh aae ||
271.e: The sovereigns were called from all the four directions and they all reached Avadhpuri

271.g: ਗਹੇ ਰਾਮ ਪਾਯੰ ਪਰਮ ਪ੍ਰੀਤ ਕੈ ਕੈ ॥
271.t: gahe raam paaya(n) param preet kai kai ||

271.g: ਮਿਲੇ ਚੱਤ੍ਰ ਦੇਸੀ ਬਡੀ ਭੇਟ ਦੈ ਕੈ ॥੬੮੦॥
271.t: mile cha'tr dhesee baddee bheT dhai kai ||680||
271.e: They all fell at the feet of Ram, exhibiting their supreme love and met him with great presents.680.
The kings presented gifts from various and beautiful maidens of elegant hair.

271.g: ਕੀਏ ਖੇਜ ਪੱਈਯੈ ਕਹੂੰ ਏਕ ਏਕੰ ॥੬੮੧॥
271.t: ke'ee khej pa'ieeyai kahoo(n) ek eka(n) ||681||
271.e: They also presented rare gems. Jewels and garments 681.
They presented winsome horses, jewels, gems, pearls as well as elephants
The chariots, diamonds, raiments and invaluable precious stones were also presented.682.
Somewhere the whit elephants bedecked with gems are being presented

271.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਬਾਜ ਰਾਜੰ ਜਰੀ ਜੀਨ ਸੰਗੰ ॥
271.t: kite baaj raaja(n) jaree jeen sa(n)ga(n) ||

271.g: ਨਚੈ ਨੱਟ ਮਾਨੋ ਮਚੇ ਜੰਗ ਰੰਗੰ ॥੬੮੩॥
271.t: nachai na'T maano mache ja(n)g ra(n)ga(n) ||683||
271.e: Somewhere the horses tightened with brocaded thick cloth are dancing exhibiting a spectacle of war. 683.

271.g: ਦਈ ਰਕਤ ਨੀਲੰ ਮਣੀ ਰੰਗ ਰੰਗੰ ॥
271.t: dhiee rakat neela(n) manee ra(n)g ra(n)ga(n) ||

272.g: ਲਖਯੋ ਰਾਮ ਕੋ ਅੱਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੀ ਅਭੰਗੰ ॥੬੮੪॥
272.t: lakhayo raam ko a'tr dhaaree abha(n)ga(n) ||684||
272.e: The kings, who presented multi-coloured red and blue gems, had a sight of Ram, the wielder of weapons and arms.684.

272.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਪਸਮ ਪਾਟੰਬਰੰ ਸ੍ਵਰਣ ਬਰਣੰ ॥
272.t: kite pasam paaTa(n)bara(n) savairan barana(n) ||

272.g: ਮਿਲੇ ਭੇਟ ਲੈ ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤੰ ਅਭਰਣੰ ॥
272.t: mile bheT lai bhaat bhaata(n) abharana(n) ||
272.e: Somewhere the kings are meeting Ram with golden colored silken raiments and various types of ornaments

272.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਪਰਮ ਪਾਟੰਬਰੰ ਭਾਨ ਤੇਜੰ ॥
272.t: kite param paaTa(n)bara(n) bhaan teja(n) ||

272.g: ਦਏ ਸੀਅ ਧਾਮੰ ਸਭੋ ਭੋਜ ਭੋਜੰ ॥੬੮੫॥
272.t: dhe seea dhaama(n) sabho bhoj bhoja(n) ||685||
272.e: Somewhere the garments shining like sun are being sent to the abode of Sita.685.

272.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਭੂਖਣੰ ਭਾਨ ਤੇਜੰ ਅਨੰਤੰ ॥
272.t: kite bhookhana(n) bhaan teja(n) ana(n)ta(n) ||

272.g: ਪਠੇ ਜਾਨਕੀ ਭੇਟ ਦੈ ਦੈ ਦੁਰੰਤੰ ॥
272.t: paThe jaanakee bheT dhai dhai dhura(n)ta(n) ||
272.e: Somewhere the ornaments shining like sun are being sent to Sita

272.g: ਘਨੇ ਰਾਮ ਮਾਤਾਨ ਕੀ ਭੇਟ ਭੇਜੇ ॥
272.t: ghane raam maataan kee bheT bheje ||

272.g: ਹਰੇ ਚਿੱਤ ਕੇ ਜਾਹਿ ਹੇਰੇ ਕਲੇਜੇ ॥੬੮੬॥
272.t: hare chi't ke jaeh here kaleje ||686||
272.e: Many ornaments and garments were sent to the mothers of Ram, seeing which many became covetous in their hearts.686.

272.g: ਘਮੰ ਚਕ੍ਰ ਚੱਕ੍ਰੰ ਫਿਰੀ ਰਾਮ ਦੋਹੀ ॥
272.t: ghama(n) chakr cha'kra(n) firee raam dhohee ||

272.g: ਮਨੋ ਬਯੋਤ ਬਾਗੋ ਤਿਮੰ ਸੀਅ ਸੋਹੀ ॥
272.t: mano bayot baago tima(n) seea sohee ||
272.e: On all the four sides, revolving the canopies, declarations were made regarding Ram and SIta also looked splendid like a decorated garden.

272.g: ਪਠੈ ਛੱਤ੍ਰ ਦੈ ਦੈ ਛਿਤੰ ਛੋਣ ਧਾਰੀ ॥
272.t: paThai chha'tr dhai dhai chhita(n) chhon dhaaree ||

272.g: ਹਰੇ ਸਰਬ ਗਰਬੰ ਕਰੇ ਪੁਰਬ ਭਾਰੀ ॥੬੮੭॥
272.t: hare sarab garaba(n) kare purab bhaaree ||687||
272.e: The kings were sent to far off places with to canopy of Ram, they smashed the pride of all and arranged festivities.687.

272.g: ਕਟਯੋ ਕਾਲ ਏਵੰ ਭਏ ਰਾਮ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
272.t: kaTayo kaal eva(n) bhe raam raaja(n) ||

272.g: ਫਿਰੀ ਆਨ ਰਾਮੰ ਸਿਰੰ ਸਰਬ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
272.t: firee aan raama(n) sira(n) sarab raaja(n) ||
272.e: In this way sufficient time elapsed in Ram’s kingdom and Ram began to rule magnificently

272.g: ਫਿਰਿਯੋ ਜੈਤ ਪਤ੍ਰੰ ਸਿਰੰ ਸੇਤ ਛੱਤ੍ਰੰ ॥
272.t: firiyo jait patra(n) sira(n) set chha'tra(n) ||

272.g: ਕਰੇ ਰਾਜ ਆਗਿਆ ਧਰੈ ਬੀਰ ਅੱਤ੍ਰੰ ॥੬੮੮॥
272.t: kare raaj aagiaa dharai beer a'tra(n) ||688||
272.e: Letters of victory were sent to all sides and under a white canopy and commanding Ram looked greatly impressive.688.

272.g: ਦਯੋ ਏਕ ਏਕੰ ਅਨੇਕੰ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਰੰ ॥
272.t: dhayo ek eka(n) aneka(n) prakaara(n) ||

272.g: ਲਖੇ ਸਰਬ ਲੋਕੰ ਸਹੀ ਰਾਵਣਾਰੰ ॥
272.t: lakhe sarab loka(n) sahee raavanaara(n) ||
272.e: Everyone was given wealth in various ways and the people saw the real personality of Ram.

272.g: ਸਹੀ ਬਿਸਨ ਦੇਵਾਰਦਨ ਦ੍ਰੋਹ ਹਰਤਾ ॥
272.t: sahee bisan dhevaaradhan dhroh harataa ||

272.g: ਚਹੂੰ ਚੱਕ ਜਾਨਯੋ ਸੀਆ ਨਾਥ ਭਰਤਾ ॥੬੮੯॥
272.t: chahoo(n) cha'k jaanayo seeaa naath bharataa ||689||
272.e: He was known on all four direction as the destroyer of the rebels of Vishnu and the lord of Sita.689.

272.g: ਸਹੀ ਬਿਸਨ ਅਉਤਾਰ ਕੈ ਤਾਹਿ ਜਾਨਯੋ ॥
272.t: sahee bisan aautaar kai taeh jaanayo ||

272.g: ਸਭੋ ਲੋਕ ਖਯਾਤਾ ਬਿਧਾਤਾ ਪਛਾਨਯੋ ॥
272.t: sabho lok khayaataa bidhaataa pachhaanayo ||
272.e: Everyone considered him as an incarnation of Vishnu and he was famous among the people as the Lord.

272.g: ਫਿਰੀ ਚਾਰ ਚੱਕ੍ਰੰ ਚਤੁਰ ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੰ ॥
272.t: firee chaar cha'kra(n) chatur cha'kr dhaara(n) ||

272.g: ਭਯੋ ਚੱਕ੍ਰਵਰਤੀ ਭੂਅੰ ਰਾਵਣਾਰੰ ॥੬੯੦॥
272.t: bhayo cha'kravaratee bhooa(n) raavanaara(n) ||690||
272.e: In all the four directions the current of Ram’s praise flowed as he , the enemy of Ravana, was known as the Supreme Soverign.690.

272.g: ਲਖਯੋ ਪਰਮ ਜੋਗਿੰਦ੍ਰਣੋ ਜੋਗ ਰੂਪੰ ॥
272.t: lakhayo param jogi(n)dhrano jog roopa(n) ||

272.g: ਮਹਾਦੇਵ ਦੇਵੰ ਲਖਯੋ ਭੂਪ ਭੂਪੰ ॥
272.t: mahaadhev dheva(n) lakhayo bhoop bhoopa(n) ||
272.e: He looked like a supreme Yogi amongst Yogis, great god anong gods and a supreme sovereign amongst kings.

272.g: ਮਹਾ ਸੱਤ੍ਰ ਸੱਤ੍ਰੰ ਮਹਾ ਸਾਧ ਸਾਧੰ ॥
272.t: mahaa sa'tr sa'tra(n) mahaa saadh saadha(n) ||
272.e: He was considered the great enemy of enemies and supreme saint amongst saints

272.g: ਮਹਾ ਰੂਪ ਰੂਪੰ ਲਖਯੋ ਬਯਾਧ ਬਾਧੰ ॥੬੯੧॥
272.t: mahaa roop roopa(n) lakhayo bayaadh baadha(n) ||691||
272.e: He was an extremely elegant personality who was the destroyer of all ailments.691.

272.g: ਤ੍ਰੀਯੰ ਦੇਵ ਤੁੱਲੰ ਨਰੰ ਨਾਰ ਨਾਹੰ ॥
272.t: treeya(n) dhev tu'la(n) nara(n) naar naaha(n) ||
272.e: He was like god for women and like a sovereign for men

272.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੋਧ ਜੋਧੰ ਮਹਾ ਬਾਹ ਬਾਹੰ ॥
272.t: mahaa jodh jodha(n) mahaa baeh baaha(n) ||
272.e: He was a supreme warrior amongst warriors amongst warriors and a great wielder of weapons amongst the weapons-wielders.

272.g: ਸ੍ਰੁਤੰ ਬੇਦ ਕਰਤਾ ਗਣੰ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਰੂਪੰ ॥
272.t: sruta(n) bedh karataa gana(n) rudhr roopa(n) ||
272.e: He was the creator of Vedas and Shiva for his devotees (ganas).

272.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੋਗ ਜੋਗੰ ਮਹਾ ਭੂਪ ਭੂਪੰ ॥੬੯੨॥
272.t: mahaa jog joga(n) mahaa bhoop bhoopa(n) ||692||
272.e: Among Yogis he was the great Yogi and of the Kings, the great King.692.

272.g: ਪਰੰ ਪਾਰਗੰਤਾ ਸਿਵੰ ਸਿੱਧ ਰੂਪੰ ॥
272.t: para(n) paaraga(n)taa siva(n) si'dh roopa(n) ||

272.g: ਬੁਧੰ ਬੁੱਧਿ ਦਾਤਾ ਰਿਧੰ ਰਿੱਧ ਕੂਪੰ ॥
272.t: budha(n) bu'dh dhaataa ridha(n) ri'dh koopa(n) ||
272.e: He was the giver of salvation, blissful, adept-like, giver of intellect and the store-house of wealth of powers

272.g: ਜਹਾ ਭਾਵ ਕੈ ਜੇਣ ਜੈਸੋ ਬਿਚਾਰੇ ॥
272.t: jahaa bhaav kai jen jaiso bichaare ||

272.g: ਤਿਸੀ ਰੂਪ ਸੌ ਤਉਨ ਤੈਸੇ ਨਿਹਾਰੇ ॥੬੯੩॥
272.t: tisee roop sau taun taise nihaare ||693||
272.e: With whatever feeling one looked towards him, he saw him in that form.693.

272.g: ਸਭੋ ਸਸਤ੍ਰਧਾਰੀ ਲਹੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਗੰਤਾ ॥
272.t: sabho sasatradhaaree lahe sasatr ga(n)taa ||

272.g: ਦੁਰੇ ਦੇਵ ਦ੍ਰੋਹੀ ਲਖੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਹੰਤਾ ॥
272.t: dhure dhev dhrohee lakhe praan ha(n)taa ||
272.e: All the weapon-wielders saw him as a specialist in weapon-warfare and all the demons who were spiteful towards gods, visualsing him as destroyer of life, hid themselves

272.g: ਜਿਸੀ ਭਾਵ ਸੋ ਜਉਨ ਜੈਸੇ ਬਿਚਾਰੇ ॥
272.t: jisee bhaav so jaun jaise bichaare ||

272.g: ਤਿਸੀ ਰੰਗ ਕੈ ਕਾਛ ਕਾਛੇ ਨਿਹਾਰੇ ॥੬੯੪॥
272.t: tisee ra(n)g kai kaachh kaachhe nihaare ||694||
272.e: With whatever feeling one thought of him, Ram seemed to him in the same colour.694.

272.g: ਅਨੰਤ ਤੁਕਾ ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
272.t: ana(n)t tukaa bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||
272.e: ANANT-TUKA BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

272.g: ਕਿਤੋ ਕਾਲ ਬੀਤਿਓ ਭਯੋ ਰਾਮ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
272.t: kito kaal beetio bhayo raam raaja(n) ||

272.g: ਸਭੈ ਸੱਤ੍ਰ ਜੀਤੇ ਮਹਾ ਜੁੱਧ ਮਾਲੀ ॥
272.t: sabhai sa'tr jeete mahaa ju'dh maalee ||
272.e: A good deal of time passed during the reign of Ram and all the enemies were conquered after great wars

272.g: ਫਿਰਯੋ ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਚਾਰੋ ਦਿਸਾ ਮੱਧ ਰਾਮੰ ॥
272.t: firayo cha'kr chaaro dhisaa ma'dh raama(n) ||

272.g: ਭਯੋ ਨਾਮ ਤਾ ਤੇ ਮਹਾ ਚੱਕ੍ਰਵਰਤੀ ॥੬੯੫॥
272.t: bhayo naam taa te mahaa cha'kravaratee ||695||
272.e: Ram’s influence spread in all the four directions and he became the Supreme Soverign.695.

272.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
272.t: bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||
272.e: BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

272.g: ਸਭੈ ਬਿੱਪ ਆਗਸਤ ਤੇ ਆਦਿ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥
272.t: sabhai bi'p aagasat te aadh lai kai ||

273.g: ਭ੍ਰਿਗੰ ਅੰਗੁਰਾ ਬਿਆਸ ਤੇ ਲੈ ਬਿਸਿਸਟੰ ॥
273.t: bhiraga(n) a(n)guraa biaas te lai bisisaTa(n) ||
273.e: All the sages including Agastya, Bhring, Angira, Vyasa, Vasishtha,

273.g: ਦੁਰਬਾਸਾ ਸਭੈ ਕਸਪ ਤੇ ਆਦ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥੬੯੬॥
273.t: dhurabaasaa sabhai kasap te aadh lai kai ||696||
273.e: Along with Vishvamitra, Valmiki, Durvasa, Kashyap and Atri came to him.696.

273.g: ਜਭੈ ਰਾਮ ਦੇਖੈ ਸਭੈ ਬਿੱਪ ਆਏ ॥
273.t: jabhai raam dhekhai sabhai bi'p aae ||

273.g: ਪਰਯੋ ਧਾਇ ਪਾਯੰ ਸੀਆ ਨਾਥ ਜਗਤੰ ॥
273.t: parayo dhai paaya(n) seeaa naath jagata(n) ||
273.e: When Ram saw all the Brahmins coming to him, then Ram, the Lord of Sita and the world ran to touch their feet.

273.g: ਦਯੋ ਆਸਨੰ ਅਰਘੁ ਪਾਦ ਰਘੁ ਤੇਣੰ ॥
273.t: dhayo aasana(n) aragh paadh ragh tena(n) ||

273.e: He gave them seats, washes their feet and all the great sages blessed him with delight.697.

273.g: ਭਈ ਰਿਖ ਰਾਮੰ ਬਡੀ ਗਿਆਨ ਚਰਚਾ ॥
273.t: bhiee rikh raama(n) baddee giaan charachaa ||

273.g: ਕਹੋ ਸਰਬ ਜੌਪੈ ਬਢੈ ਏਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥਾ ॥
273.t: kaho sarab jauapai baddai ek gra(n)thaa ||
273.e: Great discussions pertaining to divine knowledge were held between the sages and ram and if all of it is described, this granth (book) will become voluminous.

273.g: ਬਿਦਾ ਬਿੱਪ੍ਰ ਕੀਨੇ ਘਨੀ ਦੱਛਨਾ ਦੈ ॥
273.t: bidhaa bi'pr keene ghanee dha'chhanaa dhai ||

273.g: ਚਲੇ ਦੇਸ ਦੇਸੰ ਮਹਾ ਚਿੱਤ ਹਰਖੰ ॥੬੯੮॥
273.t: chale dhes dhesa(n) mahaa chi't harakha(n) ||698||
273.e: All the sages were bestowed with suitable presents on bidding farewell to them who went away to their places happily.698.

273.g: ਇਹੀ ਬੀਚ ਆਯੋ ਮ੍ਰਿਤੰ ਸੂਨ ਬਿੱਪੰ ॥
273.t: eihee beech aayo mrita(n) soon bi'pa(n) ||

273.g: ਜੀਐ ਬਾਲ ਆਜੈ ਨਹੀ ਤੋਹਿ ਸ੍ਰਾਪੰ ॥
273.t: jeeaai baal aajai nahee toh sraapa(n) ||
273.e: During this period a sage came with the corpse of his dead son and said to Ram, “If my child is not revived, I shall curse you.”

273.g: ਸਭੈ ਰਾਮ ਜਾਨੀ ਚਿਤੰ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਾਤਾ ॥
273.t: sabhai raam jaanee chita(n) taeh baataa ||

273.e: Ram ruminated about it in his mind and started towards the westerly direction in his air-vehicle.699.

273.g: ਹੁਤੋ ਏਕ ਸੂਦ੍ਰੰ ਦਿਸਾ ਉਤ੍ਰ ਮੱਧੰ ॥
273.t: huto ek soodhra(n) dhisaa utr ma'dha(n) ||

273.g: ਝੁਲੈ ਕੂਪ ਮੱਧੰ ਪਰਯੋ ਔਧ ਮੁੱਖੰ ॥
273.t: jhulai koop ma'dha(n) parayo aauadh mu'kha(n) ||
273.e: In the north-western direction a Shudra was hanging overturned in a well

273.g: ਮਹਾ ਉਗ੍ਰ ਤੇ ਜਾਪ ਪਸਯਾਤ ਉਗ੍ਰੰ ॥
273.t: mahaa ugr te jaap pasayaat ugra(n) ||

273.g: ਹਨਯੋ ਤਾਹਿ ਰਾਮੰ ਅਸੰ ਆਪ ਹੱਥੰ ॥੭੦੦॥
273.t: hanayo taeh raama(n) asa(n) aap ha'tha(n) ||700||
273.e: He was performing a penance  Ram killed him with his own hand.700.

273.g: ਜੀਯੋ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਪੁਤ੍ਰੰ ਹਰਯੋ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਸੋਗੰ ॥
273.t: jeeyo braham putra(n) harayo braham soga(n) ||

273.g: ਬਢੀ ਕੀਰਤ ਰਾਮੰ ਚਤੁਰ ਕੁੰਟ ਮੱਧੰ ॥
273.t: baddee keerat raama(n) chatur ku(n)T ma'dha(n) ||
273.e: The son of Brahmin regained his life and his agony ended. The praise of Ram spread in all the four directions.

273.g: ਕਰਯੋ ਦਸ ਸਹੰਸ੍ਰ ਲਉ ਰਾਜ ਅਉਧੰ ॥
273.t: karayo dhas saha(n)sr lau raaj aaudha(n) ||

273.g: ਫਿਰੀ ਚਕ੍ਰ ਚਾਰੋ ਬਿਖੈ ਰਾਮ ਦੋਹੀ ॥੭੦੧॥
273.t: firee chakr chaaro bikhai raam dhohee ||701||
273.e: In this way Ram was eulogized all over and the ruled over his kingdom for ten thousand years.701.

273.g: ਜਿਣੇ ਦੇਸ ਦੇਸੰ ਨਰੇਸੰ ਤ ਰਾਮੰ ॥
273.t: jine dhes dhesa(n) naresa(n) ta raama(n) ||

273.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੁੱਧ ਜੇਤਾ ਤਿਹੂੰ ਲੋਕ ਜਾਨਯੋ ॥
273.t: mahaa ju'dh jetaa tihoo(n) lok jaanayo ||
273.e: Ram conquered the kings of various countries and he was considered a great conqueror in the three worlds.
He made Bharat his ministers and made Lakshman and Shatrughan, the sons of Sumitra, his generals.702.
MRITGAT STANZA
The drum is resounding on the door of the great sage Raghuvir (Ram),
And in the whole world, in all houses and in the abode of gods, he was hailed.703.
Being known with the name of Raghunandan, ram is the lord os the world and is worshipped by the sages..
He identified the people on the earth and comforted them, removing their agony.704.
All the people considered him as the destroyer of enemies, remover of sufferings and the giver of comforts
All the city of Ayodhya is living in comfort because of his unique personality and the fearless blessings.705.
ANKA STANZA
That Ram is God, Infinite, Unconquerable and Fearless.706.

274.t: ajai hai ||707||
274.e: He is the Lord of nature, he is Purusha, he is the whole world and higher Brahman.707.

274.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
274.t: bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||

274.g: ਬੁਲਯੋ ਚਤ੍ਰ ਭ੍ਰਾਤੰ ਸੁਮਿਤ੍ਰਾ ਕੁਮਾਰੰ ॥
274.t: bulayo chatr bhraata(n) sumitraa kumaara(n) ||

274.g: ਕਰਯੋ ਮਾਥੁਰੇਸੰ ਤਿਸੇ ਰਾਵਣਾਰੰ ॥
274.t: karayo maathuresa(n) tise raavanaara(n) ||
274.e: One day Ram sent for the son of Sumitra and said to him :

274.g: ਤਹਾ ਏਕ ਦਈਤੰ ਲਵੰ ਉਗ੍ਰ ਤੇਜੰ ॥
274.t: tahaa ek dhieeta(n) lava(n) ugr teja(n) ||

274.g: ਦਯੋ ਤਾਹਿ ਅੱਪੰ ਸਿਵੰ ਸੂਲ ਭੇਜੰ ॥੭੦੮॥
274.t: dhayo taeh a'pa(n) siva(n) sool bheja(n) ||708||
274.e: In a distant land there lives a huge demon named Lavan, who has got the trident of Shiva,708.

274.g: ਪਠਯੋ ਤੀਰ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੰ ਦੀਯੋ ਏਕ ਰਾਮੰ ॥
274.t: paThayo teer ma(n)tra(n) dheeyo ek raama(n) ||

274.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੁੱਧ ਮਾਲੀ ਮਹਾ ਧਰਮ ਧਾਮੰ ॥
274.t: mahaa ju'dh maalee mahaa dharam dhaama(n) ||
274.e: Ram gave him an arrow after reciting a mantra which was a great weapon from Ram, the abode of Dharma.

274.g: ਸਿਵੰ ਸੂਲ ਹੀਣੰ ਜਵੈ ਸੱਤ੍ਰ ਜਾਨਯੋ ॥
274.t: siva(n) sool heena(n) javai sa'tr jaanayo ||

274.g: ਤਬੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਾ ਕੈ ਮਹਾ ਜੁੱਧ ਠਾਨਯੋ ॥੭੦੯॥
274.t: tabai sa(n)g taa kai mahaa ju'dh Thaanayo ||709||
274.e: Ram said to him “When you see the enemy without the trident of Shiva, then wage a war with him.”709.

274.g: ਲਯੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਤੀਰੰ ਚਲਯੋ ਨਿਆਇ ਸੀਸੰ ॥
274.t: layo ma(n)tr teera(n) chalayo niaai seesa(n) ||

274.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਪੁਰ ਜੁੱਧ ਜੇਤਾ ਚਲਯੋ ਜਾਣ ਈਸੰ ॥
274.t: tirapur ju'dh jetaa chalayo jaan ieesa(n) ||
274.e: Shatrughan taking that charmed arrows and bowing his head started for his errand and it seemed that he was going as conquerer of the three worlds

274.g: ਲਖਯੋ ਸੂਲ ਹੀਣੰ ਰਿਪੰ ਜਉਣ ਕਾਲੰ ॥
274.t: lakhayo sool heena(n) ripa(n) jaun kaala(n) ||

274.g: ਤਬੈ ਕੋਪ ਮੰਡਯੋ ਰਣੰ ਬਿਕਰਾਲੰ ॥੭੧੦॥
274.t: tabai kop ma(n)ddayo rana(n) bikaraala(n) ||710||
274.e: When he saw the enemy without the trident of Shiva, then finding an opportunity, he furiously began to wage war with him.710.

274.g: ਭਜੈ ਘਾਇ ਖਾਯੰ ਅਗਾਯੰਤ ਸੂਰੰ ॥
274.t: bhajai ghai khaaya(n) agaaya(n)t soora(n) ||

274.g: ਹਸੇ ਕੰਕ ਬੰਕੰ ਘੁਮੀ ਗੈਣ ਹੂਰੰ ॥
274.t: hase ka(n)k ba(n)ka(n) ghumee gain hoora(n) ||
274.e: After getting wounded the warriors began to run away and the crows began to caw o seeing the corpse. The heavenly damsels began to wander in the sky

274.g: ਉਠੇ ਟੋਪ ਟੁੱਕੰ ਕਮਾਣੰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
274.t: auThe Top Tu'ka(n) kamaana(n) prahaare ||

274.g: ਰਣੰ ਰੋਸ ਰੱਜੇ ਮਹਾ ਛੱਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੇ ॥੭੧੧॥
274.t: rana(n) ros ra'je mahaa chha'tr dhaare ||711||
274.e: The helmets broke with the blow of arrows and the great sovereigns were highly enraged in the battlefield.711.

274.g: ਫਿਰਯੋ ਅਪ ਦਈਤੰ ਮਹਾ ਰੋਸ ਕੈ ਕੈ ॥
274.t: firayo ap dhieeta(n) mahaa ros kai kai ||

274.g: ਹਣੇ ਰਾਮ ਭ੍ਰਾਤੰ ਵਹੈ ਬਾਣ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥
274.t: hane raam bhraata(n) vahai baan lai kai ||
274.e: That demon in great rage revolved and showered a volley of arrows on the brother of Ram

274.g: ਰਿਪੰ ਨਾਸ ਹੇਤੰ ਦੀਯੋ ਰਾਮ ਅੱਪੰ ॥
274.t: ripa(n) naas heta(n) dheeyo raam a'pa(n) ||

274.g: ਹਣਿਯੋ ਤਾਹਿ ਸੀਸੰ ਦ੍ਰੁਗਾ ਜਾਪ ਜੱਪੰ ॥੭੧੨॥
274.t: haniyo taeh seesa(n) dhrugaa jaap ja'pa(n) ||712||
274.e: The arrows which was given by Ram for the destruction of the enemy, Shatrughan discharged it on the demon, repeating the name of Durga.712.

274.g: ਗਿਰਯੋ ਝੂਮ ਭੂਮੰ ਅਘੂਮਯੋ ਅਰਿ ਘਾਯੰ ॥
274.t: girayo jhoom bhooma(n) aghoomayo ar ghaaya(n) ||

274.g: ਹਣਯੋ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਹੰਤਾ ਤਿਸੈ ਚਉਪ ਚਾਯੰ ॥
274.t: hanayo satr ha(n)taa tisai chaup chaaya(n) ||
274.e: The enemy received a wounded and while revolving, he fell down on the earth and he was killed by Shatrughan

275.g: ਗਣੰ ਦੇਵ ਹਰਖੇ ਪ੍ਰਬਰਖੰਤ ਫੂਲੰ ॥
275.t: gana(n) dhev harakhe prabarakha(n)t foola(n) ||
275.e: The gods were overjoyed in the sky and began to shower floweres

275.g: ਹਤਯੋ ਦੈਤ ਦ੍ਰੋਹੀ ਮਿਟਯੋ ਸਰਬ ਸੂਲੰ ॥੭੧੩॥
275.t: hatayo dhait dhrohee miTayo sarab soola(n) ||713||
275.e: With the killing of this malignant demon, all their agony ended.713.

275.g: ਲਵੰ ਨਾਸੁਰੈਯੰ ਲਵੰ ਕੀਨ ਨਾਸੰ ॥
275.t: lava(n) naasuraiya(n) lava(n) keen naasa(n) ||
275.e: All the saints were delighted with the destruction of the demon named Lavan

275.g: ਸਭੈ ਸੰਤ ਹਰਖੇ ਰਿਪੰ ਭੇ ਉਦਾਸੰ ॥
275.t: sabhai sa(n)t harakhe ripa(n) bhe udhaasa(n) ||
275.e: The enemies became depressed,

275.g: ਭਜੈ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਲੈ ਲੈ ਤਜਯੋ ਨਗਰ ਬਾਸੰ ॥
275.t: bhajai praan lai lai tajayo nagar baasa(n) ||
275.e: And fled away after forsaking the city

275.g: ਕਰਯੋ ਮਾਥੁਰੇਸੰ ਪੁਰੀਵਾ ਨਵਾਸੰ ॥੭੧੪॥
275.t: karayo maathuresa(n) pureevaa navaasa(n) ||714||
275.e: Shatrughan stayed in the city of Mathura.714.

275.g: ਭਯੋ ਮਾਥੁਰੇਸੰ ਲਵੰਨਾਸ੍ਰ ਹੰਤਾ ॥
275.t: bhayo maathuresa(n) lava(n)naasr ha(n)taa ||

275.g: ਸਭੈ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਗਾਮੀ ਸੁਭੰ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਗੰਤਾ ॥
275.t: sabhai sasatr gaamee subha(n) sasatr ga(n)taa ||
275.e: After destroying Lavan, Shatrughan ruled over Mathura and all the weapon-wielders gave the blessings of good wishes to him.

275.g: ਭਏ ਦੁਸਟ ਦੂਰੰ ਕਰੂਰੰ ਸੁ ਠਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: bhe dhusaT dhoora(n) karoora(n) su Thaama(n) ||

275.g: ਕਰਯੋ ਰਾਜ ਤੈਸੋ ਜਿਮੰ ਅਉਧ ਰਾਮੰ ॥੭੧੫॥
275.t: karayo raaj taiso jima(n) aaudh raama(n) ||715||
275.e: He ended all the tyrants and ruled over Mathura like Ram ruling over Avadh.715.

275.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਦੁਸਟ ਨਾਸੰ ਪਪਾਤੰਤ ਸੂਰੰ ॥
275.t: kariyo dhusaT naasa(n) papaata(n)t soora(n) ||

275.g: ਉਠੀ ਜੈ ਧੁਨੰ ਪੁਰ ਰਹੀ ਲੋਗ ਪੂਰੰ ॥
275.t: auThee jai dhuna(n) pur rahee log poora(n) ||
275.e: On destroying the tyrant, the people of all directions hailed Shatrughan  his fame spread in all the directions nicely

275.g: ਗਈ ਪਾਰ ਸਿੰਧੰ ਸੁ ਬਿੰਧੰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: giee paar si(n)dha(n) su bi(n)dha(n) prahaara(n) ||

275.g: ਸੁਨਿਯੋ ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਚਾਰੰ ਲਵੰ ਲਾਵਣਾਰੰ ॥੭੧੬॥
275.t: suniyo cha'kr chaara(n) lava(n) laavanaara(n) ||716||
275.e: And the people came to know with great zeal that demon Lavan had been killed.716.

275.g: ਅਥ ਸੀਤਾ ਕੋ ਬਨਬਾਸ ਦੀਬੋ ॥
275.t: ath seetaa ko banabaas dheebo ||
275.e: Now begins the description about the Exile of Sita :

275.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
275.t: bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||
275.e: It happened then like this and on this side Ram said to Sita with love:

275.g: ਭਈ ਏਮ ਤਉਨੈ ਇਤੈ ਰਾਵਣਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: bhiee em taunai itai raavanaara(n) ||

275.g: ਕਹੀ ਜਾਨਕੀ ਸੋ ਸੁਕੱਥੰ ਸੁਧਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: kahee jaanakee so suka'tha(n) sudhaara(n) ||

275.g: ਰਚੇ ਏਕ ਬਾਗੰ ਅਭਿਰਾਮੰ ਸੁ ਸੋਭੰ ॥
275.t: rache ek baaga(n) abhiraama(n) su sobha(n) ||

275.g: ਲਖੇ ਨੰਦਨੰ ਜਉਨ ਕੀ ਕ੍ਰਾਤ ਛੋਭੰ ॥੭੧੭॥
275.t: lakhe na(n)dhana(n) jaun kee kraat chhobha(n) ||717||
275.e: “A forest may be created, seeing which the brightness of Nandan forest (of heaven) be dimmed.”717.

275.g: ਸੁਨੀ ਏਮ ਬਾਨੀ ਸੀਆ ਧਰਮ ਧਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: sunee em baanee seeaa dharam dhaama(n) ||

275.g: ਰਚਿਯੋ ਏਕ ਬਾਗੰ ਮਹਾ ਅਭਰਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: rachiyo ek baaga(n) mahaa abharaama(n) ||
275.e: Listening to the orders of Ram, the abode of Dharma, a very beautiful garden was created

275.g: ਮਣੀ ਭੂਖਿਤੰ ਹੀਰ ਚੀਰੰ ਅਨੰਤੰ ॥
275.t: manee bhookhita(n) heer cheera(n) ana(n)ta(n) ||

275.g: ਲਖੇ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਪੱਥੰ ਲਜੇ ਸ੍ਰੋਭ ਵੰਤੰ ॥੭੧੮॥
275.t: lakhe i(n)dhr pa'tha(n) laje srobh va(n)ta(n) ||718||
275.e: That garden looked like one bedecked with gems and diamonds and before which the forest of Indra felt shy.718.

275.g: ਮਣੀ ਮਾਲ ਬਜ੍ਰੰ ਸਸੋਭਾਇ ਮਾਨੰ ॥
275.t: manee maal bajra(n) sasobhai maana(n) ||

275.g: ਸਭੈ ਦੇਵ ਦੇਵੰ ਦੁਤੀ ਸੁਰਗ ਜਾਨੰ ॥
275.t: sabhai dhev dheva(n) dhutee surag jaana(n) ||
275.e: It was thus decorated with jewels, wreaths and diamonds that all the gods had considered it as a second heaven.

275.g: ਗਏ ਰਾਮ ਤਾ ਮੋ ਸੀਆ ਸੰਗ ਲੀਨੇ ॥
275.t: ge raam taa mo seeaa sa(n)g leene ||

275.g: ਕਿਤੀ ਕੋਟ ਸੁੰਦਰੀ ਸਭੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਕੀਨੇ ॥੭੧੯॥
275.t: kitee koT su(n)dharee sabhai sa(n)g keene ||719||
275.e: Ram Chander went to abide there with Sita and many beautiful women.719.

275.g: ਰਚਯੋ ਏਕ ਮੰਦ੍ਰੰ ਮਹਾ ਸੁਭ੍ਰ ਠਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: rachayo ek ma(n)dhra(n) mahaa subhr Thaama(n) ||

275.g: ਕਰਯੋ ਰਾਮ ਸੈਨੰ ਤਹਾ ਧਰਮ ਧਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: karayo raam saina(n) tahaa dharam dhaama(n) ||
275.e: A beautiful palace was built there where Ram, the abode of Dharma,

275.g: ਕਰੀ ਕੇਲ ਖੇਲੰ ਸੁ ਬੇਲੰ ਸੁ ਭੋਗੰ ॥
275.t: karee kel khela(n) su bela(n) su bhoga(n) ||

275.g: ਹੁਤੋ ਜਉਨ ਕਾਲੰ ਸਮੈ ਜੈਸ ਜੋਗੰ ॥੭੨੦॥
275.t: huto jaun kaala(n) samai jais joga(n) ||720||
275.e: Used to sleep and enjoyed at different times in various ways.720.

275.g: ਰਹਯੋ ਸੀਅ ਗਰਭੰ ਸੁਨਯੋ ਸਰਬ ਬਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: rahayo seea garabha(n) sunayo sarab baama(n) ||

275.g: ਕਹੇ ਏਮ ਸੀਤਾ ਪੁਨਰ ਬੈਨ ਰਾਮੰ ॥
275.t: kahe em seetaa punar bain raama(n) ||
275.e: After sometimes all the women heard that Sita was pregnant, then Sita said to Ram :

275.g: ਫਿਰਯੋ ਬਾਗ ਬਾਗੰ ਬਿਦਾ ਨਾਥ ਦੀਜੈ ॥
275.t: firayo baag baaga(n) bidhaa naath dheejai ||

275.g: ਸੁਨੋ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਇਹੈ ਕਾਜ ਕੀਜੈ ॥੭੨੧॥
275.t: suno praan piaare ihai kaaj keejai ||721||
275.e: “I have wandered enough in this forest, O my lord, bid me farewell.721.

275.g: ਦੀਯੌ ਰਾਮ ਸੰਗੰ ਸੁਮਿਤ੍ਰਾ ਕੁਮਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: dheeyau raam sa(n)ga(n) sumitraa kumaara(n) ||

275.g: ਦਈ ਜਾਨਕੀ ਸੰਗ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਸੁਧਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: dhiee jaanakee sa(n)g taa ke sudhaara(n) ||
275.e: Ram sent Sita alongwith Lakshman

275.g: ਜਹਾ ਘੋਰ ਸਾਲੰ ਤਮਾਲੰ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਾਲੰ ॥
275.t: jahaa ghor saala(n) tamaala(n) bikraala(n) ||

275.g: ਤਹਾ ਸੀਅ ਕੋ ਛੋਰ ਆਇਯੋ ਉਤਾਲੰ ॥੭੨੨॥
275.t: tahaa seea ko chhor aaiyo utaala(n) ||722||
275.e: Lakshman left her in the Vihar forest, where there were lawful trees of saal and tamaal.722.

275.g: ਬਨੰ ਨਿਰਜਨੰ ਦੇਖ ਕੈ ਕੈ ਅਪਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: bana(n) nirajana(n) dhekh kai kai apaara(n) ||

275.g: ਬਨੰਬਾਸ ਜਾਨਯੋ ਦਯੋ ਰਾਵਣਾਰੰ ॥
275.t: bana(n)baas jaanayo dhayo raavanaara(n) ||
275.e: Finding herself in a desolate forest, Sita understood that Ram had exiled her

275.g: ਰੁਰੋਦੰ ਸੁਰ ਉੱਚੰ ਪਪਾਤੰਤ ਪ੍ਰਾਨੰ ॥
275.t: rurodha(n) sur u'cha(n) papaata(n)t praana(n) ||

275.g: ਰਣੰ ਜੇਮ ਵੀਰੰ ਲਗੇ ਮਰਮ ਬਾਨੰ ॥੭੨੩॥
275.t: rana(n) jem veera(n) lage maram baana(n) ||723||
275.e: There she began to weep in a fatal sound in a loud voice like a warrior being shot by an arrow on the secret parts.723.

275.g: ਸੁਨੀ ਬਾਲਮੀਕੰ ਸ੍ਰੁਤੰ ਦੀਨ ਬਾਨੀ ॥
275.t: sunee baalameeka(n) sruta(n) dheen baanee ||

275.g: ਚਲਯੋ ਕਉਕ ਚਿੱਤੰ ਤਜੀ ਮੋਨ ਧਾਨੀ ॥
275.t: chalayo kauk chi'ta(n) tajee mon dhaanee ||
275.e: The sage Valmiki heard this voice and forsaking his silence and shouting in wonder went towards Sita

275.g: ਸੀਆ ਸੰਗਿ ਲੀਨੇ ਗਯੋ ਧਾਮ ਆਪੰ ॥
275.t: seeaa sa(n)g leene gayo dhaam aapa(n) ||

275.g: ਮਨੋ ਬੱਚ ਕਰਮੰ ਦੁਰਗਾ ਜਾਪ ਜਾਪੰ ॥੭੨੪॥
275.t: mano ba'ch karama(n) dhuragaa jaap jaapa(n) ||724||
275.e: He returned to his home alongwith Sita repeating the name of Sruga with mind, speech and action.724.

276.g: ਭਯੋ ਏਕ ਪੁੱਤ੍ਰੰ ਤਹਾ ਜਾਨਕੀ ਤੈ ॥
276.t: bhayo ek pu'tra(n) tahaa jaanakee tai ||

276.g: ਮਨੋ ਰਾਮ ਕੀਨੋ ਦੁਤੀ ਰਾਮ ਤੇ ਲੈ ॥
276.t: mano raam keeno dhutee raam te lai ||
276.e: Sita bore a son there who was just a replica of Ram

276.g: ਵਹੈ ਚਾਰ ਚਿਹਨੰ ਵਹੈ ਉੱਗ੍ਰ ਤੇਜੰ ॥
276.t: vahai chaar chihana(n) vahai u'gr teja(n) ||

276.g: ਮਨੋ ਅੱਪ ਅੰਸੰ ਦੁਤੀ ਕਾਢਿ ਭੇਜੰ ॥੭੨੫॥
276.t: mano a'p a(n)sa(n) dhutee kaadd bheja(n) ||725||
276.e: He had the same colour, mask and splendour and it seemed that Ram had taken out his part and given to him.725.

276.g: ਦੀਯੋ ਏਕ ਪਾਲੰ ਸੁ ਬਾਲੰ ਰਿਖੀਸੰ ॥
276.t: dheeyo ek paala(n) su baala(n) rikheesa(n) ||

276.g: ਲਸੈ ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਰੂਪੰ ਕਿਧੋ ਦਯੋਸ ਈਸੰ ॥
276.t: lasai cha(n)dhr roopa(n) kidho dhayos ieesa(n) ||
276.e: The great sage brought up that boy who was moonlike and lookede like the sun during the day.

276.g: ਗਯੋ ਏਕ ਦਿਵਸੰ ਰਿਖੀ ਸੰਧਿਯਾਨੰ ॥
276.t: gayo ek dhivasa(n) rikhee sa(n)dhiyaana(n) ||

276.g: ਲਯੋ ਬਾਲ ਸੰਗੰ ਗਈ ਸੀਅ ਨਾਨੰ ॥੭੨੬॥
276.t: layo baal sa(n)ga(n) giee seea naana(n) ||726||
276.e: One day the sage went for Sandhya-worship and Sita taking the boy with her went to take a bath.726.

276.g: ਰਹੀ ਜਾਤ ਸੀਤਾ ਮਹਾ ਮੋਨ ਜਾਗੇ ॥
276.t: rahee jaat seetaa mahaa mon jaage ||

276.g: ਬਿਨਾ ਬਾਲ ਪਾਲੰ ਲਖਯੋ ਸੋਕੁ ਪਾਗੇ ॥
276.t: binaa baal paala(n) lakhayo sok paage ||
276.e: When the sage came out of his contemplation after the departure of Sita, he became anxious on not seeing the boy
